name: The Creative
essence: Pure, tireless creative force, like the sky that never stops turning. This is about the power to begin and to sustain, and about knowing which stage of that power you are in.

judgment.text: The Creative: a great beginning, a clear way through. Staying true to the course brings benefit.
judgment.meaning: All six lines are solid, so this is strength without any softness or hesitation in it. The four words of the Judgment (origin, success, benefit, constancy) describe the whole life of a good undertaking: it starts from a real source, it moves freely, it produces something of value, and it holds firm until the end. The omen is excellent, but it is conditional on that last word. Raw energy alone burns out or scatters. What makes it creative is that it keeps its direction. If you have an idea, a role, or a duty in front of you, this is the time to give it your full effort and to keep giving it, steadily, rather than in bursts. The lines below show that the same power must be used differently at each stage.

image.text: Heaven above, Heaven below: the sky moves on with unfailing strength. So the noble one makes themselves strong and never lets up.
image.meaning: The sky does not rest or take a day off; the sun rises, the seasons turn. Doubling the trigram stresses that this movement is continuous. The practice is not to force great feats but to cultivate a strength that renews itself each day: discipline, health, learning, integrity. Strength here is a habit, not a mood. You become reliable the way the heavens are reliable.

lines.text: A dragon lies hidden in the deep. Do not act yet.
lines.meaning: The power is real but its time has not come. Like a dragon still under the water, you have the strength and the idea, but you are not yet seen or ready. Acting now would waste it. Keep building quietly: learn, prepare, gather your resources, and let your conviction mature. This is not timidity; it is timing.

lines.text: The dragon appears in the field. It helps to go and see a great person.
lines.meaning: Your ability has come into view. You are not yet in charge, but people can now see what you can do. This is the moment to seek out someone with wider reach, a mentor, a sponsor, a person whose judgment you respect, and to let them see you clearly. The line sits in the center of the lower trigram and answers the ruler in line 5: good work done in the right place gets noticed.

lines.text: The noble one works hard all day, and at nightfall is still careful and alert. Dangerous, but no mistake.
lines.meaning: You are at the top of the lower trigram, between one level and the next, and the pressure is real. Ambition could tip into exhaustion or arrogance here. The answer is diligence with watchfulness: keep working, then review your day honestly in the evening. Success in this position draws attention and risk. If you stay conscientious, the danger passes and you will not have done wrong.

lines.text: Leaping, or staying in the depths. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You stand at a threshold where you could rise to a higher position or remain where you are and keep working below. There is no rule for this; only you can tell whether the moment is right. Both choices can be correct, provided you choose out of honesty with yourself, not vanity or fear. Test the leap. If it is not time, return to the deep without shame.

lines.text: The flying dragon is in the heavens. It helps to see a great person.
lines.meaning: This is the ruler’s place, strong and central: power and position match. Your work reaches far and others respond to it. In this fullness, it is still wise to keep company with people of real quality, to seek them out and draw them to you. Great influence is best shared with those who can match it. A rare and very favorable line.

lines.text: The dragon that overreaches will have regrets.
lines.meaning: The dragon has flown past the point where it can still connect with anyone below. When strength goes beyond its limit, it loses touch: with colleagues, with reality, with its own source. You will regret pushing further now. Know when you have arrived. Step back, share credit, let others carry part of the load. Holding on at the peak is how a peak becomes a fall.

all.text: When all the lines are nines: a flight of dragons appears with no one at the head. Good fortune.
all.meaning: When every line moves, pure strength turns toward its opposite, yielding. The image is of many dragons in the sky, none of them insisting on leading. Power is at its best when it does not need to dominate. In a team, a family, or your own character, strength combined with modesty brings good fortune: each strong person does their part without grabbing the front. Lead by not needing to be seen leading.

life.work: Commit fully and keep going, but read the stage you are in: prepare, show your ability, persevere, choose, lead, and know when to stop.
life.love: Bring energy and steadiness to the people you care for; strength that does not dominate makes others feel safe rather than overshadowed.
life.inner: Build a strength that renews itself daily through habit and honesty, not one that depends on moods or applause.

question: Which stage of the dragon am I in right now, and am I acting in a way that fits it?

name: The Receptive
essence: The power of the earth: to receive, carry, and bring to completion. This is about strength that works by responding, supporting, and nurturing rather than by initiating.

judgment.text: The Receptive: a great beginning, a clear way through, with the steady perseverance of a mare. The noble one has somewhere to go. Leading first, they lose the way; following, they find a guide. It helps to find friends in the west and south and to part from friends in the east and north. Calm, steady persistence brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: All six lines are open, so this is the perfect counterpart to The Creative. The earth does not start things; it receives the seed and turns it into a harvest. The mare is the image: strong, tireless, able to cover great distances, yet gentle and willing to be guided. If you try to take the lead now, you will go astray. If you let a clear purpose, a good leader, or the needs of the situation guide you, you will find your way. West and south, in the traditional arrangement, are the regions of the earth and of shared labor; east and north are where one stands alone before the ruler. So join with others in the work, then be willing to set that companionship aside when duty calls. Quiet persistence is fortunate.

image.text: Earth doubled: the land lies open and yielding. So the noble one, with generous character, carries all things.
image.meaning: The ground supports everything without choosing: forests and weeds, cities and graves. It is broad and it holds. The practice is to widen your capacity: to bear with people, to make room, to support what grows around you without needing to control it. Depth of character shows in what you can carry calmly. Being receptive is not weakness; it is the strength to hold.

lines.text: Frost underfoot. Solid ice is on its way.
lines.meaning: The first chill is a sign of what the season will bring. Small beginnings have their own momentum, and what starts as a hint of coldness, a minor dishonesty, or a slight drift in a relationship will grow if left alone. Notice the frost now. This is the moment when a small correction is easy. Later, the ice will be hard to break.

lines.text: Straight, square, and great. Without practice, nothing fails to benefit.
lines.meaning: This is the central line of the hexagram and expresses the earth’s nature at its purest. Straight: honest and direct. Square: steady, fair, dependable. Great: wide in scope. When you embody these, you do not need special technique or rehearsal; things work out because your character is sound. Be natural and true to your role, and trust it.

lines.text: Hidden excellence, able to stay the course. If you work in the king’s service, do not claim credit, but carry the work through to the end.
lines.meaning: You have real gifts, but now is not the time to display them. Keep them under the surface and let your conduct speak. If you serve a larger purpose, an employer, a project, a family, do the work faithfully and let the results belong to the whole. Not seeking recognition is a kind of freedom here. Finishing well is what matters.

lines.text: A sack tied shut. No blame, no praise.
lines.meaning: The times are uncertain or hostile, and openness would be risky. Keep your opinions and resources to yourself for now, like a bag with its neck tied. You will not be praised for it, but you will not be harmed or blamed either. Discretion is the right choice. Withdraw, stay quiet, and wait until the situation is safer.

lines.text: A yellow lower garment. Great good fortune.
lines.meaning: Yellow is the color of the earth and of the center; the lower garment is worn underneath and is unshowy. In a position of influence, you succeed through modesty and genuine inner quality, not display. Your refinement comes out through how you behave, not through what you claim. Real excellence that does not advertise itself is deeply trusted. A very favorable line.

lines.text: Dragons fight in the open country. Their blood is black and yellow.
lines.meaning: The yielding force has gone too far and tries to stand as an equal to the strong. Black is the color of heaven, yellow of earth: both sides are wounded. When someone who should support insists on ruling, or a relationship turns into a power struggle, everyone bleeds. This is a warning of serious harm. Return to your proper role before the fight costs both sides.

all.text: When all the lines are sixes: it helps to persevere for the long term.
all.meaning: When every line moves, receptivity turns toward strength, and the danger is that it loses its footing. What keeps it sound is lasting constancy: holding to what is right over a long time, not just in one good moment. Steady, patient faithfulness becomes a strength in its own right. If you keep going, consistently and without fuss, the yielding becomes firm and the outcome is good.

life.work: Support the leader or the plan rather than competing with it; do thorough, reliable work, finish what you start, and let credit fall where it will.
life.love: Listen, make room, and be dependable; caring well sometimes means following the other person’s lead instead of steering.
life.inner: Practice being open and steady without losing your own center; notice small early signs, and let your quality show in conduct rather than words.

question: Where would it serve me to follow and support rather than to lead?

name: Difficult Beginnings
essence: The tangled, effortful start of something new, like a sprout pushing through hard ground. This is about getting through confusion at the beginning without forcing or giving up.

judgment.text: Difficult beginnings: a great start, a clear way through, and benefit in staying true. Do not rush to go somewhere. It helps to appoint helpers.
judgment.meaning: The character shows a sprout struggling up through the soil. Thunder below is moving up; water above is the abyss, danger. New energy meets resistance. This is a fertile kind of chaos: everything is stirring, nothing yet has form. The omen is fundamentally good, as with The Creative, but the way through is not to charge ahead. Too much is unsettled; a premature move could lose everything. Instead, stay committed and build your support. The old text says to set up feudal lords, meaning to put trusted people in charge of parts of the work. If you are starting a project, a relationship, or a new stage of life, expect confusion, keep faith with your aim, and bring in help.

image.text: Clouds and thunder: the image of difficult beginnings. So the noble one sorts the tangled threads and weaves them into order.
image.meaning: Before rain, clouds gather and thunder rolls; the air is charged and nothing has broken yet. The noble one does not wait passively in this tension but starts to organize: separating threads, setting up a warp and weft. When things are new and messy, the practice is to create structure: priorities, roles, a plan for the next step. Order made at the beginning lets the storm become rain that helps things grow.

lines.text: Hesitating, circling around. It helps to remain steady and true. It helps to appoint helpers.
lines.meaning: At the very start, you meet an obstacle and cannot move forward. Do not take this as a reason to give up, and do not force it. Hold to your intention, stay humble, and gather the right people around you. This strong line under weak ones is a natural leader in a low place: by treating others with respect, you win their support. Help is what moves you now.

lines.text: Difficulties pile up. Horse and carriage part ways. Not a robber: a suitor. The young woman stays faithful and does not commit. After ten years, she commits.
lines.meaning: A tempting offer of help or union appears when you are struggling. It is not hostile, but it is not the right one: accepting it would bind you to the wrong connection. Line 2 is meant for line 5, not for the strong line close by. Stay true to your real purpose, even if that means waiting a long time. The right bond will come. Patience here protects your integrity.

lines.text: Hunting deer without a guide, you only lose your way in the forest. The noble one sees the signs and gives it up. Going on brings humiliation.
lines.meaning: You are pursuing something in unfamiliar territory with no one who knows the ground. The forest swallows you. You can see where this is heading: further effort only gets you more lost. The wise move is to stop, admit you lack the knowledge or the guide, and turn back. Insisting will embarrass you. Find expertise before you go on.

lines.text: Horse and carriage part ways. Seek union. Going forward brings good fortune; everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: You cannot do this alone, and an opportunity for partnership is present. The difference from line 2 is that this connection is the right one: line 4 corresponds with the strong line 1. Swallow your pride and reach out. Asking for or accepting help now is not weakness. Acting on it brings good fortune, and things open up on every side.

lines.text: Difficulty in giving out your bounty. Small, steady correctness brings good fortune; forcing great things brings misfortune.
lines.meaning: You are in a position of influence and have resources to share, but conditions make it hard for your generosity or good intentions to reach people. There is mistrust or obstruction around you. Do not try to push a grand plan through now; that goes badly. Work patiently and in small ways, earning trust bit by bit. Gradual progress is fortunate.

lines.text: Horse and carriage part ways. Tears of blood flow.
lines.meaning: At the end of the difficulty, you have lost heart and stopped trying. You are stuck and grieving, unable to go forward or back. This is the bitterness of giving up in the middle of hardship. The line is painful, but it is also a warning: despair locks you in. If you can, seek help, take one small step, and remember that every beginning is hard.

life.work: Expect early setbacks; do not launch everything at once, but set up structure, delegate, and find people who know the terrain.
life.love: New relationships need patience and the right fit; do not grab at the first offer of comfort, and do not quit when it gets confusing.
life.inner: Tolerate the mess of becoming; keep faith with your direction while you sort one thread at a time.

question: What one piece of order, or one helper, would make this beginning less tangled?

name: Youthful Folly
essence: The not-knowing of the beginner and the right relationship between learner and teacher. This is about how to learn well, how to teach well, and the price of insincere questions.

judgment.text: Youthful folly: a way through. I do not seek out the young fool; the young fool seeks me. At the first asking, I answer. Asking a second or third time is disrespect, and to disrespect I give no answer. Staying true is beneficial.
judgment.meaning: A spring rises at the foot of a mountain, still unsure where to flow. This is inexperience, not stupidity, and it can grow into wisdom. But learning has rules. The student must come to the teacher, not the reverse; nobody can be taught who does not want to learn. The oracle itself speaks here: ask once, sincerely, and you will get an answer. Ask again and again because you dislike the reply, and you are no longer seeking guidance but testing it; you will get nothing. The omen is good if the learner is earnest and the teacher is consistent. Whether you are learning something or guiding someone, be sincere, patient, and firm.

image.text: A spring flows out at the foot of the mountain: the image of youth. So the noble one acts with decisiveness and nurtures character.
image.meaning: The water at the mountain’s base does not stay still: it keeps moving, fills every hollow, and eventually finds its course. The practice is to be thorough and persistent in what you do, while cultivating your inner quality. Learning is less about one leap of understanding and more about steady flow. Fill each gap before moving on, and let action and character grow together.

lines.text: To develop the young fool, it helps to apply discipline. Remove the shackles. But to keep on this way brings humiliation.
lines.meaning: At the start, some firmness is needed: clear rules, accountability, consequences that make learning serious. Discipline is meant to free the learner from bad habits, not to imprison them. If correction becomes constant pressure or punishment, it backfires and shames everyone. Set firm standards, then loosen them as soon as the lesson has taken hold.

lines.text: To bear with fools kindly brings good fortune. To take a wife brings good fortune. The son is able to run the household.
lines.meaning: This strong central line is the true teacher of the hexagram. It deals with the inexperienced gently and with patience, the way a mature person accepts a partner’s imperfections or a parent trusts a capable child with responsibility. You can carry others now, and you are ready to take charge. Generosity toward the shortcomings of others is fortunate and earns their trust.

lines.text: Do not take a woman who, seeing a man of gold, loses hold of herself. Nothing is gained.
lines.meaning: This describes someone who throws themselves at whatever seems powerful or rich, losing their own dignity. As a learner, it is the person who imitates whoever impresses them instead of truly learning. Do not chase status or attach yourself to the glitter of others, and do not take on someone who does. Such a connection leads nowhere. Keep your self-respect.

lines.text: Folly that is tangled up and cut off. Humiliation.
lines.meaning: This weak line has no strong neighbors and no strong partner: it is surrounded by its own kind and far from anyone who could guide it. Stuck in fantasies and unreal ideas, it will meet a hard and humiliating reality. If you notice that you are isolated from honest advice, the embarrassment is a lesson. Sometimes the teacher can only let the learner run into the wall.

lines.text: Childlike folly. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: In the ruling place, this is the beginner who is open, humble, and teachable: the kind of not-knowing that becomes wisdom. This line looks to the strong teacher in line 2. When you approach a problem without pretending to know it all, asking real questions and listening to the answers, you learn quickly and people want to help you. Openness is fortunate.

lines.text: In punishing folly, it does not help to act like a bandit. It helps to guard against bandits.
lines.meaning: Sometimes folly must be stopped firmly. But the purpose of correction is to protect, not to take revenge or vent anger. If you become harsh or cruel in punishing someone’s mistake, you become the very problem you are guarding against. Set clear limits, prevent harm, and stop there. Strictness serves order only when it stays measured.

life.work: Admit what you do not know, ask good questions once and listen to the answers, and if you lead or mentor, be patient but consistent.
life.love: Accept a partner’s inexperience with kindness; avoid people, or impulses in yourself, that lose dignity in front of power or money.
life.inner: Cultivate the beginner’s mind: be sincere in what you ask, including of this oracle, and do not ask again just to get a better answer.

question: What am I really trying to learn here, and am I willing to accept the answer I already got?

name: Waiting
essence: Waiting with confidence for what cannot be hurried, like waiting for rain. This is about using the waiting well: keeping calm, nourishing yourself, and staying ready.

judgment.text: Waiting. With sincerity and trust, there is brightness and a way through. Staying true brings good fortune. It helps to cross the great river.
judgment.meaning: Heaven, strong and eager to move, lies below Water, the danger ahead. The strength is not stuck; it simply has to wait for the right moment. The key word is sincerity: inner confidence that the outcome will come. If you wait with clear eyes, neither fooling yourself nor fretting, the situation becomes bright and opens up. This is not passivity. Because you prepare and stay true while you wait, you will be able to cross the great river, to take on the big challenge, when the time is right. Rain cannot be hurried by worry. Do not force a decision before it is ripe, and do not give up because it is slow.

image.text: Clouds rise up into the sky: the image of waiting. So the noble one eats and drinks, and is at ease and cheerful.
image.meaning: Clouds have gathered; the rain will fall in its own time. There is nothing to do to hasten it. So the noble one takes care of themselves: eats, drinks, rests, keeps their spirits up. This is not indulgence but preparation. When you cannot act yet, keep your body and mind in good condition, enjoy what is in front of you, and save your strength for the moment it is needed.

lines.text: Waiting in the outskirts. It helps to keep to what lasts. No mistake.
lines.meaning: The danger is still far off, like a storm beyond the horizon. Do not let anticipation pull you out of your ordinary life. Keep to your routines, your work, your usual pace. Nothing calls for drastic action yet. Steadiness now is right, and you will not go wrong by staying where you are and living normally.

lines.text: Waiting on the sand. There is some gossip. In the end, good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are closer to the water now, and the ground is less firm. Small frictions appear: criticism, rumors, disagreements. Do not get drawn into arguments or try to defend yourself against every remark. Stay calm and generous, in the center as this line is. The talk will pass, and things end well.

lines.text: Waiting in the mud brings the bandits.
lines.meaning: You have moved forward too soon and stuck yourself right at the edge of the danger. In this exposed position, you invite trouble: opponents, setbacks, people ready to take advantage. You put yourself here. Recognize it and act with great care: stay alert, be cautious, and do not make it worse. Serious harm can still be avoided by prudence.

lines.text: Waiting in blood. Get out of the pit.
lines.meaning: You are now inside the danger, in a fight or a crisis that is truly serious. This is no time for struggle or heroics. Hold still, yield to what you cannot change, and wait for the opening to get out. By not resisting blindly and keeping calm, you can climb out of the hole. Accepting the situation is how you survive it.

lines.text: Waiting with food and wine. Staying true brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: In the middle of difficulty, there is a pause: a meal, a breath, a moment of peace. This strong central line in the ruler’s place knows how to use it. Enjoy the respite and gather your strength, but do not forget your purpose or lose your discipline. Good things are coming, and patience combined with steadiness brings them.

lines.text: You fall into the pit. Three guests arrive unbidden. Treat them with respect, and in the end, good fortune.
lines.meaning: The waiting is over, and the danger has come. It seems there is no way out. Then help arrives from an unexpected quarter, in a form you did not ask for and may not recognize as help. Welcome it. Treat the visitors with courtesy even if they do not look like rescuers. Being open to an unforeseen turn changes everything, and the end is good.

life.work: Do not force the deal or the launch; prepare thoroughly and keep your energy up so you can act well when the moment comes.
life.love: Give things time to unfold and trust what is genuine between you; worry and pressure will not speed it up.
life.inner: Practice calm confidence: take care of yourself, enjoy ordinary things, and stay alert without anxiety.

question: What am I waiting for, and how can I wait well instead of anxiously?

name: Conflict
essence: A clash of wills where you feel you are right and are blocked. This is about how to handle disputes: stop halfway, seek a fair judge, and avoid carrying a fight to the bitter end.

judgment.text: Conflict. You are sincere, but you are blocked. Stopping carefully halfway brings good fortune; going all the way brings misfortune. It helps to see a great person. It does not help to cross the great river.
judgment.meaning: Heaven above rises and Water below sinks: the two pull apart. This is the shape of a dispute. Inside is danger and cunning, outside is stubborn strength. You may be convinced you are right, and you may be; that is what makes the situation so tempting. But if you push the conflict to the end, even winning will cost you dearly, and the omen says plainly it goes badly. The wise course is to pause midway, stay alert, and look for a settlement. Bring in someone fair and respected who can judge impartially. This is not a time for big ventures or risky undertakings; your energy is tied up in the dispute, and unity with others is lacking.

image.text: Heaven and water go in opposite directions: the image of conflict. So the noble one, in every undertaking, thinks carefully at the beginning.
image.meaning: The sky moves up and away; water flows down. Once they part, they never meet again. Many conflicts grow from vague beginnings: unclear agreements, unspoken expectations, roles nobody defined. The practice is prevention. When you start something with others, take time to clarify the terms, the responsibilities, the hopes. Careful thought at the start removes most of the reasons to fight later.

lines.text: If you do not drag the matter out, there is a little gossip. In the end, good fortune.
lines.meaning: The conflict is only beginning, and you are in a weak position. The best thing is to let it drop early. There may be a few words exchanged, some criticism, a bruised feeling. That is small. Do not escalate or insist on the last word. By not perpetuating the quarrel, you let it fade, and things end well.

lines.text: You cannot win the dispute. You return home and slip away. The people of your town, three hundred households, suffer no harm.
lines.meaning: You face a stronger opponent: the ruler in line 5 is beyond your reach. Pride wants to fight, but that would bring harm not only on you but on everyone connected to you. Withdraw in time. Retreating here is not cowardice; it protects your people and yourself. Accept the setback and look after those who depend on you.

lines.text: Living on old virtue, you hold firm. Dangerous, but in the end, good fortune. If you serve a king, do not seek accomplishments.
lines.meaning: Keep to what is rightly yours, what you have earned and inherited, rather than grabbing more. You are in a precarious spot and others may try to take even that. Staying modest and steady is the way through. If you work for someone else, do the work without seeking fame or credit; recognition is a source of conflict now. Holding back secures your position.

lines.text: You cannot win the dispute. You turn back, accept what is right, and change your attitude. Peace in staying true. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are strong enough to fight and could push your advantage against a weaker party, but you realize it would not be right. Instead, you turn around, accept the order of things, and change your mind. Finding peace by letting go of a dispute you could have won is a sign of real strength. Good fortune comes from that inner turn.

lines.text: Bringing the dispute before him: great good fortune.
lines.meaning: This is the just arbiter, strong and central in the ruling place. If you are in a dispute and right is on your side, take it to someone fair and powerful who can settle it, a mediator, a court, a respected authority. If you are that person, judge without partiality. Fair arbitration resolves the conflict, and the outcome is very good.

lines.text: Even if a leather belt of honor is granted to you, by the end of the morning it is taken away three times.
lines.meaning: You fought to the very end and won. The prize, a ceremonial belt, a title, a victory, is yours. But a triumph won through conflict is never secure; it keeps being challenged and snatched away, again and again. You will not have peace. Recognize that winning this way brings no lasting honor. Settle rather than conquer.

life.work: Clarify agreements in writing at the start; in a dispute, seek mediation and a fair settlement rather than total victory.
life.love: Being right is not worth the relationship; stop an argument halfway, and talk expectations through before they harden into grievances.
life.inner: Notice your urge to win; ask whether pushing on serves you, and be willing to change your attitude.

question: What would a fair, impartial person advise me to do about this conflict?

name: The Army
essence: An organized force gathered under one capable leader. This is about mobilizing people for a hard task with discipline, a just cause, and seasoned leadership.

judgment.text: The Army. Staying true, with a mature leader: good fortune, and no mistake.
judgment.meaning: Water is hidden inside Earth, like groundwater, or like soldiers drawn from the ordinary population. There is one strong line, in the second place, among five yielding ones: a single commander in the field, supported by the ruler in line 5 who trusts him. An army is dangerous power; used badly, it destroys. So two things are needed. The cause must be right, and the leader must be experienced and respected, someone people follow willingly. With both, a hard collective effort succeeds, and you will not be blamed for using force. In modern terms, this is any time you must mobilize people: a team under pressure, a campaign, a crisis response. Organize well, lead by example, and keep your aim just.

image.text: Water within the earth: the image of the army. So the noble one is generous to the people and gathers a great following.
image.meaning: Groundwater is a great reserve hidden in the soil, ready when needed. Likewise a state’s strength lies in its people, who must be cared for in times of peace so that they will rally in times of need. The practice is to look after those who might one day stand with you: be generous, fair, and present. Loyalty is built long before you ask for it.

lines.text: The army must set out in good order. If not, misfortune, however good the cause.
lines.meaning: At the start of any collective effort, discipline and clear purpose come first. A team without rules, roles, or an agreed plan will fall apart at the first test, whatever its intentions. Get the structure right before you march. If you go out in disorder, even success will be costly and failure likely. Order at the beginning is everything.

lines.text: In the midst of the army. Good fortune, no mistake. The king gives his commands three times.
lines.meaning: This is the commander, the only strong line, at the center of the troops. He shares the hardships of his people and holds the full trust of the ruler in line 5, who honors him repeatedly. If you lead, be among your team, not above it. Your authority rests on both the support of those above and the trust of those with you. Very favorable.

lines.text: The army may carry corpses in the wagon. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: Leadership has slipped into the wrong hands, or too many people are giving orders, and the result is defeat. A weak line in a strong place, overreaching, it pretends to command. If authority is divided or claimed by someone unfit, the effort fails, with real losses. Clarify who leads, and if it is not you, do not seize it. This goes badly.

lines.text: The army retreats and makes camp. No mistake.
lines.meaning: The enemy is too strong, or the ground is wrong. A sensible general does not throw troops at a hopeless battle; he falls back and waits. Withdrawal now is not defeat but good judgment. Pull back, regroup, and preserve your forces for a better moment. You will not be blamed for avoiding a fight you cannot win.

lines.text: There is game in the field. It helps to seize it. No mistake. Let the eldest son lead the army; if the younger son does, they cart off corpses. Even staying the course brings misfortune.
lines.meaning: Something has invaded your field, and you must act to defend it: the action is justified. But the ruler must choose the right leader, the experienced one, and then let them do the job. If you put an unqualified person in charge, or meddle and divide command, even a just campaign ends in disaster. Choose well, delegate fully, and fight only to defend.

lines.text: The great ruler gives his decrees, founding states and granting houses. Do not use small people.
lines.meaning: The campaign is over and it is time to reward people and build the peace. Those who served well are given responsibility and resources. But be careful: people who were useful in a fight are not all suited to govern. Do not hand lasting power to those with small, self-serving minds. After success, choose carefully whom you trust with the future.

life.work: Organize a hard effort with clear roles and one trusted leader; make sure the goal is fair and do not divide command.
life.love: In a family or household under strain, someone needs to lead calmly and fairly; care for people in good times so they rally in hard ones.
life.inner: Bring discipline to your scattered impulses: one clear aim, a sense of order, and a just reason for any struggle.

question: Is my cause just, and is the right person leading this effort?

name: Holding Together
essence: People gathering around a center and holding together like water on the earth. This is about joining the right group or person, or becoming a center others can rely on, and doing so in time.

judgment.text: Holding together: good fortune. Consult the oracle again: is there greatness, lasting worth, and steadiness? Then no mistake. Those who were unsettled are now coming. Whoever comes late meets misfortune.
judgment.meaning: Water lies on the earth and flows together, filling every low place and joining into one body. One strong line, in the ruler’s place, is surrounded by yielding lines that gather around it. This is the moment when people unite: around a leader, a cause, a family, a partnership. The omen is good. But anyone who would be the center must examine themselves honestly, a second inquiry, to ask whether they have the quality and constancy that union demands. If so, there is no fault. Those who hesitated are now joining. Do not wait too long: when the community has formed, the latecomer finds the door closed, and that goes badly.

image.text: Water on the earth: the image of holding together. So the ancient kings founded the many states and kept close ties with their lords.
image.meaning: Water does not stand apart from the ground; it rests on it and sinks in. The early kings built their realm the same way: by establishing many local centers and keeping warm, personal relationships with each one. The practice is to maintain your connections actively. A network, a family, or an organization holds together through ongoing care, not just through structure.

lines.text: Hold to them with sincerity and trust. No mistake. Sincerity like a full clay bowl. In the end, good fortune comes from elsewhere as well.
lines.meaning: The basis of any true union is honesty. A plain clay vessel filled to the brim is the image: no decoration, just real content. If your loyalty and feeling are genuine, not dressed up or calculated, people will sense it. Good fortune then arrives from unexpected sources too, beyond the people you approached. Be sincere first; the rest follows.

lines.text: Holding together from within. Staying true brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: This central line corresponds with the ruler in line 5. You respond to a call that matches who you are. You join because it is right for you, not out of eagerness to please or fear of being left out. Union from the inside keeps your dignity intact. Stay true to yourself in the connection, and it will be fortunate.

lines.text: You hold together with the wrong people.
lines.meaning: Your companions here do not belong to your true path, and the bond itself is not sound. The line stands among weak lines and has no proper connection. Getting close to people who are not good for you leads you away from yourself. You can be friendly, but do not give yourself over to this association. Keep a little distance and look for the right ties.

lines.text: Holding together outwardly as well. Staying true brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: This line stands right beside the ruler. It is right to show your support openly now, to stand publicly with the leader or the person you believe in. Your loyalty need not stay private. Being visibly committed to the right center, while keeping your own integrity, is fortunate.

lines.text: A shining example of holding together. The king hunts with beaters on three sides only and lets the game that runs ahead escape. The townspeople need no warnings. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: This is the ruler, the true center. In the old royal hunt, one side was left open, so animals that wished to flee could go. A real leader does not trap or pressure people into joining; whoever comes does so freely, and whoever leaves is allowed to go. Because there is no coercion, people trust and need no orders or threats. Draw people by openness.

lines.text: Holding together, but without a head. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: The time for joining has passed, or there is no proper center to join. Hesitating too long, you find yourself on the outside. Or a union started without a clear beginning, a leader, or a shared foundation, and it cannot hold. This goes badly. If there is still time, commit now; if not, accept the loss and learn when to act next time.

life.work: Join or build a team around a clear, trustworthy center, and commit in time rather than waiting to see which way things go.
life.love: Let your bonds rest on sincerity; give freely and leave others free, and do not delay too long in saying yes to what is right.
life.inner: Ask honestly whether you are steady and worthy enough to be the center others gather around, and what you truly belong to.

question: Who or what do I truly belong with, and am I joining sincerely and in time?

name: Small Taming
essence: A small, soft force holds back a great one for a while. Real progress is near but not yet possible, so you work by gentle influence and careful preparation rather than by force.

judgment.text: Small Taming. There is success. Thick clouds gather from our western lands, but no rain falls yet.
judgment.meaning: Five strong lines are held in check by a single yielding line in the fourth place: the small restrains the great. Wind, soft and moving, blows over Heaven, the strong; it can slow it but cannot master it. The image of dense clouds with no rain describes a tension that has built up and has not yet broken. The rain will come, but not today. Success is promised, though of a modest kind. This is not a time for decisive action or big moves. Your influence works through tact, persuasion and patience. Keep your aims clear, take care of details, and let pressure gather naturally. Forcing the release now would only scatter what is building. Accept that you can shape events only a little, and use that little well.

image.text: Wind drifts across the sky above Heaven: Small Taming. The noble one refines the outward expression of their character.
image.meaning: Wind can move clouds but cannot change the sky. It works on surfaces, not foundations. In the same way, when you cannot achieve anything large, you can still polish how you present yourself: your manners, your craft, the quality of your work and words. This small, patient cultivation is not trivial. It prepares you so that when the moment for greater action arrives, you meet it with grace and skill.

lines.text: Returning to your own path. How could that be a mistake? Good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are a strong line at the start, and your instinct is to push ahead. But you meet resistance and choose to go back to your own way instead of forcing the issue. That is wise. Turning back here is not defeat; it keeps you true to yourself and out of a struggle you would lose. Retreat to what you know is right, regroup, and wait. There is no blame in this, only good fortune.

lines.text: Drawn back, you return along with others. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: You would like to press forward, but you can see that others who are like you are turning back too, and you let yourself be led along with them. You are in the center of the lower trigram, so you judge the moment well. Going with good company rather than charging off alone keeps you safe. This is not weakness; it is good sense about timing and alliances. Good fortune.

lines.text: The spokes fall out of the wagon. Husband and wife glare at each other.
lines.meaning: Here the strong line tries to push forward despite the restraint, and the vehicle breaks down. The image of a quarrelling couple shows a partnership where the weaker side ends up controlling the stronger, and both resent it. You are trying to force progress when conditions do not allow it, and the result is friction and breakdown. Stop pushing. Repair the relationship and the means of moving before you try to go anywhere.

lines.text: If you are sincere, bloodshed is avoided and fear departs. No mistake.
lines.meaning: This is the single yielding line that holds back all the strong ones, a weak minister restraining powerful forces. That is a dangerous position. What protects you is sincerity: honest, transparent intent that others can trust. You do not have the power to compel anyone, so you must rely on truthfulness and good advice. Do that, and danger and anxiety fall away. No mistake.

lines.text: Sincere and bound together with others, you share your wealth with your neighbor.
lines.meaning: You are the strong ruler in the center of the upper trigram, and your loyalty binds people to you. Because you are faithful and generous, your resources are not yours alone; you use them for those around you, and they in turn support you. Mutual trust multiplies strength. Share what you have, keep your word, and stand by your allies. This kind of partnership is what makes the small taming work.

lines.text: The rain has come and things come to rest. The accumulated virtue carries the load. Persisting now, even for the yielding, is dangerous. The moon is nearly full. If the noble one sets out, misfortune.
lines.meaning: The long-awaited release has arrived: the clouds have finally broken. Effort and patience have built something real. But this is exactly the moment to stop. The gentle force that achieved the result should not keep pressing, and the moon nearly full warns that what is at its peak soon wanes. Be content with what has been gained. Pushing for more, or starting a new venture now, would go badly.

life.work: Progress is real but slow; focus on preparation, details and persuasion rather than bold moves, and do not force a breakthrough before it is ripe.
life.love: Influence your partner gently and honestly rather than by pressure; small acts of care do more now than big confrontations.
life.inner: Practice patience with a tension that has not yet resolved, and use the waiting to refine yourself.

question: Where are you trying to force rain from clouds that are still gathering?

name: Treading Carefully
essence: You must step near something powerful and dangerous. Good manners, clear awareness of your place, and calm care let you pass without harm.

judgment.text: Treading on the tiger’s tail. It does not bite. Success.
judgment.meaning: The lake, joyful and yielding, walks behind Heaven, strong and commanding. The weak follows close behind the strong, so close that it steps on the tiger’s tail. Yet the tiger does not bite, because the one treading is good-natured, respectful and light of foot. This is a situation of real risk: a demanding boss, a volatile person, a delicate negotiation, a powerful institution. You cannot avoid contact, but you can manage it. Know where you stand, behave with courtesy, keep your step cheerful and careful, and you will come through well. The omen is success, but only because conduct is right. Treading is about how you carry yourself when the margin for error is small.

image.text: Heaven above, the lake below: Treading. The noble one distinguishes high from low and so settles the hearts of the people.
image.meaning: Heaven is high and the lake is low, and both are content in their places. Order that is clear and fair brings peace of mind. When people know what is expected and who carries which role, they stop jostling and grasping. The practice here is to be clear about positions and boundaries, including your own, and to act accordingly. This is not rigid hierarchy for its own sake but the steadiness that comes from everyone knowing where they stand.

lines.text: Plain treading. Going forward, no mistake.
lines.meaning: You start out simply, without ambition to impress or climb. You are not trying to be anything but yourself, doing what is in front of you. That simplicity is your protection. When you move forward without hidden agendas or a hunger for status, you make no enemies and no errors. Stay modest in your aims and honest in your steps. Go ahead; there is no blame.

lines.text: Treading a path that is level and smooth. For the quiet, solitary person, persistence brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: You walk an even road in the center, keeping to the middle way. You do not need the crowd’s approval or the noise of competition. Like someone content in a quiet life, you are free of the pressures that push others into risky moves. Keep to your own steady course, undistracted by the scramble around you. Steadiness brings good fortune.

lines.text: The one-eyed thinks they can see; the lame thinks they can walk. They tread on the tiger’s tail and it bites. Misfortune. A soldier acts as if he were a great lord.
lines.meaning: This yielding line sits in a strong place and overrates itself. You believe you see clearly and can stride ahead, but your vision and footing are both limited. Pushing forward with false confidence provokes the danger, and it strikes back. The soldier pretending to be a ruler is someone taking on a role beyond their strength. Be honest about your limits. Reckless boldness here goes badly.

lines.text: Treading on the tiger’s tail. With caution and wariness, in the end, good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are a strong line in a yielding place, right next to the ruler, so you are close to power and danger. You do step on the tiger’s tail, but you know it, and you proceed with care, even fear. That alertness saves you. Undertake what you must, but carefully, watching every reaction. Respect the risk instead of dismissing it, and things turn out well in the end.

lines.text: Resolute treading. Persisting is dangerous.
lines.meaning: You hold the ruler’s place and you are strong and decisive. You see what must be done and you step firmly. That resolve is needed, but it carries danger: you may push ahead without listening, or forget that you too can be bitten. Act with determination, but stay aware of the risk you carry. Firmness without caution is hazardous. Be resolute and keep your eyes open.

lines.text: Look at the path you have trodden and examine the signs. If it has come full circle, supreme good fortune.
lines.meaning: The journey is over and it is time to look back. How did you conduct yourself? What were the results of your actions? Your conduct is judged by its consequences. If, on review, the path has been sound from start to finish, the outcome is excellent. Take stock honestly. Learn from the whole course of events, and let that understanding guide what you do next.

life.work: Handle powerful people and risky situations with courtesy, clarity about your role and careful steps; do not overreach.
life.love: Tread gently around sensitive matters; respect, good humor and tact keep a tense relationship safe.
life.inner: Know your own place and limits without shame, and move through danger with calm attention.

question: What tiger are you walking behind, and how lightly are you stepping?

name: Peace
essence: Heaven and Earth meet and exchange: everything flows, things grow, people cooperate. It is a time of flourishing, to be used well and not taken for granted.

judgment.text: Peace. The small goes, the great comes. Good fortune and success.
judgment.meaning: Earth is above and Heaven below. Heaven’s energy naturally rises and Earth’s naturally sinks, so they move toward each other and meet. This is communion: high and low, strong and receptive, are in contact and exchange. The three strong lines are within and the yielding lines are outside, so strength is at the core and gentleness at the surface. The petty and unhelpful are on their way out; what is great and good is arriving. This is a favorable period for almost anything: building, collaborating, starting, reconciling. Things go smoothly because communication is open. Enjoy it, but use it actively to lay strong foundations. Peace is a season, and seasons change.

image.text: Heaven and Earth unite: Peace. The ruler shapes and completes the way of Heaven and Earth and supports their proper order, so as to help the people.
image.meaning: When nature’s forces are in harmony, people still have to work with them, like farmers dividing the year into seasons and planting at the right time. The leader’s task is to give form to good conditions: to organize, regulate and direct them so they actually benefit everyone. In your life, this means turning a good situation into lasting structures, habits and agreements rather than simply enjoying the ease.

lines.text: When the reed grass is pulled up, its roots come with it, each with its kind. Setting out brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: In good times, capable people draw one another forward; when one rises, those connected to them rise too, like a clump of grass pulled up with its roots. You are not acting alone. Go ahead with your plans and bring your allies with you. Starting something now, together with like-minded people, will go well.

lines.text: Bearing with the rough and unrefined, fording the river without a boat, not neglecting what is far, letting cliques fall away: this way you keep to the middle and win honor.
lines.meaning: You are a strong line at the center, corresponding with the ruler above. The task is generous leadership. Be tolerant of people who are crude or unskilled; be bold enough to act decisively when needed; remember distant matters and people; and refuse to play favorites. These four qualities together make you trusted. Breadth of heart, plus courage, plus fairness, is the true middle way.

lines.text: There is no plain without a slope, no going without a return. Staying steady through hardship, no mistake. Do not grieve over this truth; enjoy the good fortune you already have.
lines.meaning: You stand at the top of Heaven, where the lower trigram meets the upper one. Peace is at its height, and every height implies a descent. Do not be naive about it: change will come. But do not be anxious either. Stay faithful and steady when difficulty arrives and you will not go wrong. Meanwhile, savor what is good now, with gratitude and without clinging.

lines.text: Fluttering down, not boasting of wealth, they come together with their neighbors, unguarded and sincere.
lines.meaning: The yielding lines above descend naturally to meet the strong ones below, like birds coming down to the ground. Those in high places mix with those below without pride or display, and without suspicion. Connection here is based on genuine trust, not calculation or self-interest. Meet people simply and openly, without flaunting your position or keeping your guard up. Real community forms this way.

lines.text: King Di Yi gives his younger sister in marriage. Blessings follow, and supreme good fortune.
lines.meaning: An ancient king married his royal sister to a man of lower rank, and she accepted his household as her own. The ruler here is a yielding line that responds to the strong second line below. Power that humbles itself and joins with those beneath it creates lasting harmony and happiness. If you hold the stronger position, bend toward others and honor them. Such a union is deeply blessed.

lines.text: The city wall falls back into the moat. Do not send in the army. Issue your orders only within your own town. Persisting brings humiliation.
lines.meaning: The wall was built from earth dug out of the moat, and now it collapses back into it. Peace has turned toward decline, and what was built returns to where it came from. Fighting against this would make things worse. Do not try to force order with power. Look after your own circle, keep your word close to home, and accept the turn. Stubbornly clinging to the old state of affairs brings shame.

life.work: Conditions are favorable: collaborate, launch, and build solid structures while things flow easily, and include others in your success.
life.love: Open, easy exchange makes this a good time to deepen bonds; meet your partner on equal terms and without pride.
life.inner: Enjoy the good season with gratitude, and prepare calmly for the fact that it will change.

question: How can you turn this time of ease into something that will last?

name: Standstill
essence: Heaven and Earth pull apart and nothing flows between them. When the wrong people hold sway, you keep your integrity, withdraw from what is corrupt, and wait for the tide to turn.

judgment.text: Standstill. The wrong people are in charge. This does not favor the noble one’s steady course. The great goes, the small comes.
judgment.meaning: Heaven is above and Earth below. Heaven rises, Earth sinks, and so they move away from each other. Nothing meets, nothing is exchanged, and life stalls. The yielding lines are inside and the strong outside, so the core is weak and the strength is all on the surface. Small, self-serving forces gain ground while what is great withdraws. This can describe an organization, a society, or a relationship where honest communication has broken down. Trying to push your vision through now will not work and may compromise you. The best course is to keep your principles, decline to collude, and wait. Stagnation is not permanent. The omen is unfavorable for action, but not for character.

image.text: Heaven and Earth do not join: Standstill. The noble one draws their worth inward to escape difficulty, and does not let themselves be honored with reward.
image.meaning: When the powers that be are out of touch with ordinary life, being prominent is dangerous and being rewarded can make you complicit. The wise response is to keep your talents and convictions quietly to yourself for now. Do not seek office, praise or payment from a corrupt system. Remain inwardly strong and outwardly modest, so that you stay free and clean until better times allow you to act.

lines.text: When the reed grass is pulled up, its roots come with it, each with its kind. Persistence brings good fortune and success.
lines.meaning: The same image as in Peace, but here it means withdrawing together. When things are going wrong, a person of principle draws back, and those like them follow. You are at the very start, and you can still choose not to join in. Step away along with others who share your values. Holding firm to what is right brings good fortune and, eventually, success.

lines.text: They bear with things and flatter. For the small person, good fortune. For the great person, standstill brings success.
lines.meaning: The yielding center line goes along with those in power, swallowing its objections. For people who only want to get ahead, accommodating and flattering works for now. But if you hold to higher standards, do not play that game. Accept the blockage rather than buying your way through it. Your patience and integrity in the face of stagnation will be what brings you success later.

lines.text: They bear shame.
lines.meaning: This weak line sits at the top of the lower trigram, in a place it has not earned. Those who climbed by unworthy means begin to feel the shame of it, even if no one has called them out. If this describes you, notice that inner discomfort; it is the start of a turn. If you see it in others, understand that their position is hollow. Shame here is a sign that things are beginning to change.

lines.text: Acting on a higher mandate, no mistake. Companions share in the blessing.
lines.meaning: The standstill is past its midpoint, and a strong line now appears in the upper trigram. Someone with a true calling and the right authority can begin to restore order. If you act from genuine principle and not personal ambition, you are not at fault, and those who join you will share the benefits. Make sure your mission is legitimate; then step forward, and bring good people with you.

lines.text: The standstill comes to an end. Good fortune for the great person. “It might fail, it might fail.” Bind it fast to a clump of mulberry.
lines.meaning: The strong ruler brings the stagnation to a close, and better times begin. But the right person in charge does not assume success. Constantly saying “this could still fall apart” keeps you alert, and that wariness is what makes things secure, like tying something to the deep-rooted mulberry. Celebrate the turn, but strengthen your foundations and do not relax your vigilance.

lines.text: The standstill is overturned. First stagnation, then joy.
lines.meaning: Standstill cannot last forever; at its end it flips over. But it does not end by itself. Someone has to act to overturn it. You are at the top, and the moment has come to finish the old blockage completely. After a long period of frustration, the change brings real relief and gladness. Take the final step needed, and let the new period begin.

life.work: In a blocked or compromised environment, do not seek promotion or credit; protect your integrity, keep your skills sharp, and wait for a change.
life.love: When communication has broken down, do not force it; keep faith with your values and allow time and distance to do their work.
life.inner: Hold your convictions quietly and refuse to be corrupted, trusting that stagnation always gives way.

question: What would it mean to keep your integrity intact while nothing seems to move?

name: Fellowship
essence: People united by a shared purpose and open dealing achieve great things. Fellowship must be public and inclusive, not a closed circle of favorites.

judgment.text: Fellowship among people out in the open country. Success. It is favorable to cross the great river. It is favorable for the noble one to keep steady.
judgment.meaning: Fire rises toward Heaven, and Heaven itself moves upward: they share a direction. The single yielding line in the second place, at the center of the inner trigram, corresponds with the strong ruler in the fifth, and all the strong lines gather around it. That is the picture of fellowship. The key words are “in the open”: real community happens out in the wide country, not behind closed doors. It is based on goals everyone can see and share, not on private loyalties or factions. With such fellowship you can take on great tasks, the crossing of the great river. But it requires a clear, principled leader who keeps the group oriented by what is right, not by mere sentiment. Then success follows.

image.text: Heaven joined with fire: Fellowship. The noble one organizes people by clans and distinguishes things by their kinds.
image.meaning: Fire burns upward toward the sky and lights it. Brightness and strength go together. Yet real fellowship is not formless. A healthy community recognizes differences: people have different roles, backgrounds and gifts. Unity comes from arranging these clearly and fairly, so that each finds their place in the whole. Practice seeing distinctions clearly without letting them become divisions.

lines.text: Fellowship at the gate. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You are just stepping out of your door, at the very start of joining with others. Nothing is hidden yet; there are no secret deals or private loyalties. Fellowship begun openly, in full view, is sound. Approach people with good will and transparency. Meeting others at the threshold, on equal terms, is a good beginning. There is no blame.

lines.text: Fellowship within the clan. Regret.
lines.meaning: This yielding line, the heart of the hexagram, connects only with its own: family, friends, a familiar circle. Fellowship that is limited to your own group easily turns into faction, favoritism and exclusion. It feels comfortable but leads to regret. Look beyond your inner circle. Ask whether your loyalties are narrow and whether others are being left out. True community is wider than kinship.

lines.text: Hiding weapons in the thicket, climbing the high hill. For three years, no rising up.
lines.meaning: Here fellowship has broken down into mistrust. You suspect others, conceal your intentions, and watch from a height, waiting to strike. But the opposition is stronger than you, and so nothing happens for years. Distrust breeds more distrust. Ask yourself if the hostility is justified. Hidden scheming will not bring the union you want. It only keeps you stuck and alone.

lines.text: Climbing up on the wall, they cannot attack. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: The conflict has gone as far as standing on the wall, ready to attack. But at this point you realize the attack cannot succeed and is not right. Stopping here and turning back is a sign of growing wisdom. Choosing reconciliation over aggression, after nearly going to war, leads to good fortune. Step back from the fight. Recognizing your limits opens the way to real fellowship.

lines.text: Those in fellowship first weep and lament, then they laugh. After great struggles, they meet.
lines.meaning: Two people, or two sides, who truly belong together are separated by obstacles and suffer from it. The ruler in the fifth place and its partner in the second must overcome what lies between them. It takes real effort and grief. But because their bond is genuine, they break through and are joyfully reunited. If you face painful separation from someone you are truly linked with, persevere; the meeting will come.

lines.text: Fellowship in the meadow beyond the town. No regret.
lines.meaning: You are at the far edge of things, outside the town, where fellowship is broad but loose. There is no deep, close bond here, and no great cause to unite for. Still, you are in contact with others, and there is nothing to regret. This is a modest connection, honest but distant. Accept it for what it is, and do not expect more than it can offer.

life.work: Build teams around clear, shared goals and open communication; avoid cliques and back-room deals, and you can achieve something big together.
life.love: Bonds grow strong through openness and common purpose; beware of closing ranks only with family or old friends.
life.inner: Widen your sense of who belongs, and examine where suspicion or narrow loyalty is keeping you apart.

question: Is your sense of “us” open enough to include the people you need?

name: Great Possession
essence: You hold much: resources, influence, talent, success. Great possession is fortunate when it is held with modesty, clarity and a sense of duty to what is good.

judgment.text: Great Possession. Supreme success.
judgment.meaning: Fire, bright and clear, shines high above Heaven, strong and creative. The sun stands at the top of the sky and lights everything. A single yielding line holds the ruler’s place, and all the strong lines respond to it. This is a picture of abundance gathered around a center that is gentle, not domineering. Great wealth and influence come to someone who leads with modesty and clarity rather than force. The judgment is unusually simple: supreme success. Things go very well. But possession brings responsibility. The question is not how much you have but how you hold it and what you do with it. Inner strength and outward clarity, used generously, keep this fortune sound.

image.text: Fire high above Heaven: Great Possession. The noble one curbs what is wrong and furthers what is good, in obedience to Heaven’s generous will.
image.meaning: When the sun is high, everything is visible, both good and bad. Having power and resources means you can actually do something about what you see. The wise person uses abundance to hold back harm and support what is good. This is not self-righteousness; it is aligning your strength with the larger order of things. Possession becomes a blessing when it serves something beyond yourself.

lines.text: No contact with what is harmful, and so no mistake. Stay mindful of difficulty, and there will be no mistake.
lines.meaning: Prosperity is only beginning and has not yet been tested. You have not been drawn into arrogance, waste or the problems that wealth brings. Keep it that way. The way to stay clear of error is to remember that abundance has its own difficulties. Do not get careless. Keep your feet on the ground, remain aware of risks, and you will avoid blame.

lines.text: A big wagon for loading. There is somewhere to go. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You are a strong line in the center, responding to the ruler. Like a large, sturdy cart, you can carry a great deal. Your capacity is matched by an objective: you know where to take what you carry. Resources are meant to be used and moved toward a goal, not hoarded. Take up the load and go. There is no blame in using your strength this way.

lines.text: A prince offers it to the Son of Heaven. A small person cannot do this.
lines.meaning: A noble lord puts his wealth at the service of the king and the whole realm. Someone with a narrow, selfish outlook could not do that; they would cling to their gains. If you have significant resources or talent, offer them to a greater cause, to your community or the common good. That generosity makes your abundance meaningful. Keeping it all for yourself would harm you.

lines.text: Not making a display of abundance. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You stand close to the ruler, surrounded by the richness of the time. The temptation is to compete, show off, or try to outshine those above you. Resist it. Hold your wealth and power without flaunting them, and keep a clear sense of distinction between yourself and others. Humility and restraint keep you safe in a position where envy and rivalry could arise. No blame.

lines.text: Their sincerity binds people together, and their dignity inspires respect. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: This is the ruler of the hexagram: a yielding line in the place of power. It governs not by force but by sincerity, and others respond with trust. Yet gentleness alone would invite people to take advantage, so it must be paired with dignity. Be open, warm and honest, but also firm and composed. That combination of trust and authority brings good fortune.

lines.text: Blessed by Heaven. Good fortune. Nothing that is not favorable.
lines.meaning: At the top of great abundance, you still honor what is higher than yourself. You have wealth but you are not possessed by it; you remain open, faithful and respectful of the wise. That is why Heaven itself supports you. Everything works out. When fullness is held with humility and devotion to what is right, the blessing is complete. Enjoy it with gratitude.

life.work: Success and resources are available; use them for a clear purpose and for the wider good, and lead through clarity rather than domination.
life.love: Share generously and lead with warmth, but keep your dignity; abundance in love means giving, not possessing.
life.inner: Hold your gifts lightly and with gratitude, remembering they are entrusted to you.

question: What do you hold in abundance, and what is it for?

name: Modesty
essence: True modesty is not self-effacement but inner substance that does not need to show off. It balances excess and lack, and it lets you carry things through to the end.

judgment.text: Modesty. Success. The noble one carries things through to completion.
judgment.meaning: A mountain is hidden within the earth. The mountain is high, yet here it lies below the level ground, giving its height away. That is modesty: real stature that does not set itself above others. The only strong line sits at the top of the lower trigram, accomplished but staying low. Modesty succeeds because the natural way of things favors it: high places erode, low places fill up, and people warm to those who do not exalt themselves. It is not weakness or false humility. It is the steadiness of someone who knows their worth and does not need to advertise it. Such a person can see a task through to the end, because they are not distracted by ego. Success, quietly lasting.

image.text: Within the earth, a mountain: Modesty. The noble one reduces what is too much and adds to what is too little; weighing things, they make them even.
image.meaning: Earth brings the mountain down to its own level. The practice is balance and fairness. Take from excess and give to lack. Do not let anything, whether wealth, pride, attention or effort, pile up too high in one place. In relationships, in teams and in your own habits, look for what is overweighted and what is neglected. Modesty, at its heart, is the art of evening things out.

lines.text: Modest about one’s modesty, the noble one crosses the great river. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are at the lowest place and do not even make a show of your humility. This kind of unpretentious, unassuming manner wins cooperation and trust. With it you can take on difficult undertakings, the great river, because no one feels threatened or crossed by you. Approach big tasks simply and without fuss. Let your work speak. Good fortune.

lines.text: Modesty that makes itself heard. Persistence brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are at the center of the lower trigram, and your modesty is genuine and deep. Because it comes from your heart, it shows, and others notice and respond. You do not need to proclaim yourself; your character speaks through your words and manner. Keep being who you are, consistently. Such authentic humility brings good fortune.

lines.text: Modesty that has earned merit. The noble one carries things through. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: This is the only strong line, the heart of the hexagram. You have truly accomplished something and gained recognition, and here lies the test: will fame go to your head? If you keep working and do not rest on your laurels or demand credit, people will support you. Hard work combined with humility lets you complete what you started. Good fortune.

lines.text: Nothing that is not favorable for modesty that shows itself in action.
lines.meaning: You stand just above the hardworking line and near the ruler. Modesty here is not passive. It means actively helping, giving credit to the one doing the work, and responding properly to those above and below. Do not hide behind humility or use it as an excuse for inaction. Put modesty into practice: do your part, support others, defer where it is due. Everything works out.

lines.text: Not boasting of wealth, they join with their neighbors. It is favorable to attack and set things right. Nothing that is not favorable.
lines.meaning: You hold the ruler’s position without boasting of power or riches, and so people stand with you. But modesty is not the same as softness. When someone refuses to cooperate or does real harm, it is right to act firmly and even forcefully to correct things. Being humble does not mean letting wrong go unchallenged. Act decisively, without arrogance. All goes well.

lines.text: Modesty that makes itself heard. It is favorable to set armies marching, to bring order to your own city and country.
lines.meaning: At the end of modesty, it can tip into a name or reputation for humility. True modesty now turns inward: it disciplines yourself and your own household rather than blaming others. Put your own house in order first. Use strength on your own faults and the disorder close to you, not on outsiders. That is where effort is truly needed and well spent.

life.work: Do excellent work without seeking the spotlight, give others credit, and follow projects through to the end; this builds lasting trust.
life.love: Balance giving and receiving; avoid one-sidedness, and let warmth show without needing to be admired.
life.inner: Know your worth quietly, and keep looking for what in you is overgrown and what is neglected.

question: Where in your life is something piled too high, and where is something lacking?

name: Enthusiasm
essence: Energy bursts from the ground like thunder in spring and moves people. Enthusiasm rightly channeled gathers others and gets things moving; misused, it becomes self-indulgence or delusion.

judgment.text: Enthusiasm. It is favorable to appoint helpers and to set the armies marching.
judgment.meaning: Thunder, the arousing, rises from Earth, the yielding. After winter’s stillness, the first thunder of spring stirs everything into life. The single strong line in the fourth place is the source of movement, and all the yielding lines respond to it with willing devotion. Enthusiasm here means a shared readiness, a mood that carries people with it. That is why it is the right time to enlist helpers and set great efforts in motion. People follow gladly when the leader’s movement is in tune with their own nature and needs. The key is accord: enthusiasm works because it goes with the grain of things, as nature moves with the seasons. Inspire rather than command, and things fall into place.

image.text: Thunder comes roaring out of the earth: Enthusiasm. The ancient kings made music to honor merit, and offered it in splendor to the Supreme Lord, with their ancestors present.
image.meaning: Music is the purest expression of shared feeling: it moves people, unites them, and lets them express what words cannot. The old kings used music and ritual to celebrate goodness and connect the living with the divine and the ancestors. Enthusiasm is at its best when it lifts people toward something higher and binds a community together. Look for what genuinely inspires you and others, and give it form.

lines.text: Enthusiasm that trumpets itself. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: You are low in position but have a powerful connection above, and you boast about it. Showing off your enthusiasm or your connections, especially from a weak position, invites resentment and leads to bad outcomes. Excitement that is self-centered and noisy turns others away. Keep your satisfaction to yourself. Bragging about good fortune you have not earned goes badly.

lines.text: Firm as a rock. Not waiting a whole day. Persistence brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: While everyone else is swept up in the mood, you stay steady as stone. You are not carried off by excitement or flattery. Because you are clear-headed, you see the first signs of where things are heading and act immediately, without waiting until the end of the day. Stay grounded and act promptly on what you recognize. Steadfastness brings good fortune.

lines.text: Enthusiasm that looks upward brings regret. Hesitating also brings regret.
lines.meaning: You are gazing up at the source of enthusiasm and waiting for it to carry you. Depending on someone else for your own energy and direction leads to regret. But hanging back and missing the moment also leads to regret. Do not just look to others for inspiration or approval. Make your own decision, and make it in time.

lines.text: The source of enthusiasm. Great things are achieved. Have no doubt. Friends gather around you as hair is gathered by a clasp.
lines.meaning: You are the strong line that moves everyone: the one who inspires. Because you act from confidence and without hesitation, great things are possible. Do not doubt yourself or others. Your sincerity draws people together and holds them, like a clasp holding hair. Trust your vision, stay open and honest, and others will join you. This is a time to lead.

lines.text: Chronically ill, yet not dying.
lines.meaning: You hold the ruler’s position but are weak, and pressed hard by a strong line beneath you. You are under constant strain, which prevents you from enjoying or wasting yourself in enthusiasm. Paradoxically, that pressure keeps you alive. Continual difficulty can be a safeguard against complacency. You may not be at your best, but you endure. Keep going.

lines.text: Deluded enthusiasm. But if, once it is complete, you change course, no mistake.
lines.meaning: You are at the very top, lost in excitement that has become blind. You have been carried away by the mood and no longer see clearly. Still, it is not too late. Once things have run their course, if you wake up and change direction, you can avoid blame. Look honestly at where your enthusiasm has taken you. A sober turnaround now keeps the error from becoming permanent.

life.work: It is a good time to rally people and launch initiatives; inspire through genuine conviction, but stay alert to hype and overexcitement.
life.love: Shared joy brings you closer; express your feelings, but do not let infatuation blind you to who the other person really is.
life.inner: Let what genuinely moves you give you energy, while keeping a steady, clear head beneath the excitement.

question: Is your enthusiasm moving you toward something real, or simply carrying you along?

name: Following
essence: Following is about choosing well whom and what you follow, and adapting to the time without losing yourself. People follow freely only someone who first knows how to follow.

judgment.text: Following. Great and sweeping success. It pays to stay true to what is right. Then there is no mistake.
judgment.meaning: The lower trigram is Thunder, movement; the upper is Lake, joy. Something stirs and others respond gladly: this is following that comes from willing agreement, not force. The text promises great success, but it adds a condition. Following is only good when it is joined to integrity. To follow a fashion, a crowd or a charismatic person for comfort or gain leads astray; to follow what is right, and to adapt to what the moment truly needs, brings no blame.
