The same holds if you lead. People will follow you only if you are willing to serve the situation, to listen and to bend. So ask what deserves your loyalty now, give yourself to it wholeheartedly, and stay clear about your principles while you do.

image.text: Thunder in the middle of the lake: the image of Following. The noble one, when evening comes, goes indoors to rest and recover.
image.meaning: In late autumn the thunder sinks into the lake and goes quiet, following the turn of the season. The practice is to follow the natural rhythm of the day and the year: work when it is time to work, and when darkness comes, stop, go home and rest. Adapting to the time is not weakness. Forcing activity against it wears you out and makes you a poor guide for anyone else.

lines.text: The standard changes. Staying true brings good fortune. Go out of your own gate to meet people, and you will achieve something.
lines.meaning: Your position or your point of reference is shifting, and you need to adapt. Hold on to your core, and the change will go well. The key is to step outside your familiar circle. Do not follow only those who already agree with you or belong to your group. Talk with all kinds of people, hear opposing views, and judge them on their merit. Openness of this kind is what makes the change productive.

lines.text: If you cling to the little boy, you lose the strong man.
lines.meaning: You cannot follow everything at once, and what you attach yourself to decides what you lose. Here the danger is choosing the small, easy or immature option, the comfortable friendship, the quick reward, and thereby losing the connection that could really help you grow. Look honestly at who and what you are holding on to. If it keeps you small, it is costing you something better.

lines.text: If you cling to the strong man, you lose the little boy. In following, you find what you seek. It pays to remain steady.
lines.meaning: This is the better choice: you attach yourself to what is mature and worthwhile, and you must let go of something lesser, perhaps an old habit, a shallow pleasure or a familiar crowd. That loss is real, and you may feel it. But by following the right thing you will get what you are truly after. Stay steady in the choice and do not drift back.

lines.text: Following brings a catch. Persisting in this way is dangerous. If you are sincere and walk the right path with clear understanding, how could there be blame?
lines.meaning: You have influence, and people are starting to follow you, or you are gaining from following others. The danger is that the gain is for yourself: flatterers gather, or you start to overshadow the person you serve. Pushing on with that motive turns out badly. The cure is honesty about your aims. If you act sincerely, keep your loyalty to the right cause, and see the situation clearly, you avoid the trap.

lines.text: Sincere in following the good. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: The ruling line, strong and centered, gives its trust to what is excellent and admirable. This is following at its best: you recognize what is truly good, whether a person, a value or a calling, and commit to it with your whole heart. Such sincerity is rewarded. If you are in a leading role, it means you welcome good people and good advice rather than surrounding yourself with yes-sayers.

lines.text: Held fast and bound to it, and then tied tighter still. The king makes an offering on the Western Mountain.
lines.meaning: At the top, following has become an unbreakable bond. Someone who wanted to withdraw is held by others who will not let them go, or a person is bound to a cause so deeply that it becomes sacred. The king’s offering on the mountain shows this tie reaching beyond the personal into something of lasting meaning. Accept the bond. Your loyalty now carries weight for others, even if you once thought of stepping away.

life.work: Choose carefully whom you follow and what projects you commit to, then serve them fully; if you lead, earn loyalty by listening and adapting.
life.love: Relationships flourish when each person is willing to follow the other at times; avoid clinging to what keeps you small.
life.inner: Adapt to the time and rest when it is time to rest, without giving up your principles.

question: What am I following now, and does it deserve my loyalty?

name: Repairing the Spoiled
essence: Something has been spoiled through neglect, often handed down from those before you. Now is the time to face it and set it right, with thought before and after.

judgment.text: Repairing what has been spoiled. Great success. It pays to cross the great river. Before you start, take three days; after you start, take three days.
judgment.meaning: The character shows a bowl with worms breeding in it: rot that has grown from neglect. The trigrams agree. Wind is trapped below a still Mountain, so the air goes stale. Yet the omen is very good, because decay that is recognized can be repaired, and the work leads to a fresh start. Crossing the great river means taking on a real, demanding task rather than avoiding it. The three days before and after mean care. First understand how things went wrong; then, once the new course begins, watch that it holds and does not slide back. Do not just blame the past or patch the surface. Find the cause, act decisively, and follow through.

image.text: Wind blows low beneath the mountain: the image of Repairing. The noble one stirs the people and strengthens their character.
image.meaning: The wind at the foot of the mountain stirs everything up and sets it moving, while the mountain gives stability. Repair needs both. First you shake loose what has gone stagnant, in a family, a team or yourself, and get people moving again. Then you nourish what is good in them so the renewal lasts. Stirring without nourishing only creates unrest; nourishing without stirring leaves the rot in place.

lines.text: Setting right what the father spoiled. If there is such a son, the late father is free of blame. Danger, but in the end good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are dealing with problems that were inherited: old patterns from your family, or habits built into an organization before you arrived. They have not yet hardened, so they can still be fixed. If you take them on, the past is redeemed rather than condemned. It is risky, since changing tradition unsettles people, and you must be aware of that. Proceed carefully, and the outcome will be good.

lines.text: Setting right what the mother spoiled. Do not be too rigid.
lines.meaning: The damage here comes from weakness or indulgence rather than from hard error, and it touches tender feelings. Forcing a correction harshly would hurt people and fail. Be gentle and tactful. This line is strong and sits in the center, in correspondence with the weak ruler above, so your strength must serve with consideration. Repair what is needed without humiliating anyone, and accept that some things change slowly.

lines.text: Setting right what the father spoiled. There will be a little regret, but no great mistake.
lines.meaning: You are tackling the problem with energy, maybe too much. A strong line in a strong place can overdo it, cause friction or step on toes, and you will have small regrets. Still, it is far better to act too vigorously against decay than not at all. Accept the bumps, apologize where you went too far, and keep going. No serious harm comes from it.

lines.text: Tolerating what the father spoiled. If you go on like this, you will meet with shame.
lines.meaning: You see the problem but put up with it, out of weakness, politeness or a wish not to rock the boat. Letting it slide only lets it grow, and later you will be embarrassed that you did nothing. This line is weak and has no support from below. Admit that the issue needs action. If you cannot fix it alone, find help, but do not simply look away.

lines.text: Setting right what the father spoiled. You win praise for it.
lines.meaning: The ruler’s place, held by a yielding line, supported by the strong line below. You cannot redo everything single-handedly, but you can lead the renewal well by drawing on capable people. Correcting old faults this way earns respect and recognition. The repair succeeds and is seen to succeed, and the past is honored even as it is reformed.

lines.text: Not serving kings or lords, the person sets a higher aim for their own work.
lines.meaning: At the top, outside the action, someone chooses not to engage in public affairs or in fixing the world’s messes, and turns instead to their own integrity and deeper values. This is not laziness or contempt. It is a deliberate choice that, for now, your task lies in cultivating yourself and keeping standards alive. Do it with real purpose, so your example becomes its own kind of repair.

life.work: Face the neglected problems in a project or organization: understand the causes, fix them decisively, and check that the fix holds.
life.love: Old family patterns or wounds can be healed; be firm with what is harmful but gentle with the people involved.
life.inner: Look at what you inherited, habits and beliefs, and take responsibility for renewing it rather than blaming the past.

question: What has been spoiled through neglect in my life, and what is its real cause?

name: Approach
essence: Strength is rising and the good is drawing near. It is a time of hopeful growth and of meeting others warmly, while remembering that every spring turns to autumn.

judgment.text: Approach. Great and sweeping success. It pays to stay true. When the eighth month comes, there will be misfortune.
judgment.meaning: Two strong lines push up from below into four yielding ones: the light is growing, as in the weeks after midwinter. Approach also means a superior coming close to those below, to lead and care for them. The omen is excellent: things move forward, people are receptive, and you can achieve a great deal if you stay honest and steady. But the text adds a warning. Growth does not last forever, and in the eighth month the trend turns. The point is not gloom but foresight. Use the favorable time well, and prepare now for the decline that will follow, so it does not catch you off guard.

image.text: Earth above the lake: the image of Approach. The noble one never tires of teaching and is boundless in tolerating and protecting the people.
image.meaning: The land bordering a lake rises over the water and comes near it from above. Just as the lake is inexhaustibly deep and the earth holds everything it touches, the wise person approaches others with inexhaustible willingness to teach and with a generosity wide enough to accept and protect everyone. When you are in a position to influence people, give freely of what you know and exclude no one.

lines.text: Approaching together. Staying true brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: The rising strength begins to reach those above, and they respond. Good people are drawn together and move forward jointly. You are supported, and your influence starts to grow. The thing to watch is that you do not get swept along by the momentum. Keep to what is right, and the shared advance will bring good fortune.

lines.text: Approaching together. Good fortune, and everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: Strong and central, this line corresponds with the ruler above. Your approach meets real support from the top. Few readings are as positive: you can move forward with confidence. Still, the full hexagram warns that what rises will also fall. Make use of the good time without assuming it is permanent, and you will not be shaken when circumstances change.

lines.text: Sweet and easy approach. Nothing is gained. If you are troubled by it, there is no mistake.
lines.meaning: Here the approach is too comfortable: charm, flattery, easy promises, or a careless sense that everything is going your way. This brings no real benefit. The line sits at the top of the joyous lower trigram, prone to complacency. The remedy is to notice it and feel concern. Once you take the situation seriously and correct your attitude, the error is cleared.

lines.text: Complete approach. No mistake.
lines.meaning: This yielding line sits in its proper place and corresponds directly with the strong first line. It is the image of someone in a high position who genuinely reaches out to capable people below, without prejudice. Draw near openly to those you can help and those who can help you. The connection is right and sincere, and there is nothing to blame in it.

lines.text: Wise approach. This is fitting for a great ruler. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: The ruler is yielding but central, and corresponds with the strong second line. The wisdom of a leader lies in not trying to do everything personally: choose able people, trust them, and let them work. Knowing what to delegate and to whom is the right way to approach a great task. Lead in this way and the result is good.

lines.text: Generous approach. Good fortune, no mistake.
lines.meaning: At the top, someone who has already reached a high place or has stepped back turns again toward the world with a warm, great-hearted attitude. Experienced people return to help those coming after them. Offer your experience freely and kindly, without needing anything in return. This brings good fortune and leaves nothing to regret.

life.work: Things are moving your way; push forward, mentor others, and plan now for the downturn that will eventually come.
life.love: Draw near with real warmth and patience; avoid smooth words that lack substance.
life.inner: Enjoy the season of growth without complacency, and keep your attention awake.

question: How can I make the most of this rising time while preparing for when it turns?

name: Contemplation
essence: Contemplation means looking deeply and being looked at. You see the whole situation clearly, and your own conduct becomes an example others watch.

judgment.text: Contemplation. The hands have been washed, but the offering is not yet made. Full of trust, the people look up in reverence.
judgment.meaning: The picture is of a sacred ceremony at the moment before the offering, when the priest has washed and everyone is gathered and attentive. That moment of collected reverence is more powerful than the offering itself. In the hexagram, two strong lines stand high above four yielding ones, like a tower that sees far and is seen from far away. If you are in a visible role, your influence comes not from orders but from the seriousness and sincerity others can see in you. And to influence wisely, you must first look: survey the whole situation calmly, understand the people and the forces at work, and let clarity rather than haste guide you.

image.text: Wind moves over the earth: the image of Contemplation. The ancient kings traveled through the regions, observed the people, and gave them teaching.
image.meaning: Wind blowing across the land reaches everywhere and bends the grass as it passes. The good ruler likewise went out to see how people actually lived, and only then shaped guidance to fit. The practice is to go and look for yourself before deciding: observe firsthand, listen, understand real conditions. Then your influence, like the wind, touches everyone in a way they can receive.

lines.text: A child’s way of looking. For ordinary people, no mistake. For the noble one, shameful.
lines.meaning: At the bottom, far from the center of things, you see only the surface, as a child would. That is understandable for someone with no responsibility. But if you are meant to lead or decide, such a shallow view is not good enough. Do not settle for first impressions or other people’s summaries. Make the effort to understand what is really going on.

lines.text: Peeping through the crack of a door. Favorable for a woman’s steadiness.
lines.meaning: You see only a narrow slice of the situation, from a limited, sheltered position. In the old context this suited someone whose life was within the household. For you, it means accepting that your viewpoint is partial. That is fine for a private matter, but do not mistake it for the whole picture. Before judging others or large decisions, open the door wider.

lines.text: Contemplating my own life, I decide whether to advance or to retreat.
lines.meaning: At the turning point between inner and outer, the question is what you should do next. The answer comes from looking honestly at yourself: your actions, their effects, your real capacities. Do not look outside for direction now. Self-examination, not wishful thinking or pressure from others, shows whether it is time to go forward or step back.

lines.text: Contemplating the light of the kingdom. It pays to be the guest of the king.
lines.meaning: Close to the ruler, you can see how a well-ordered enterprise works and what makes it flourish. This is an invitation: offer your abilities to those who lead it, and serve as an honored guest, contributing your gifts while keeping your independence. A good organization or mentor is worth joining. Recognizing such light and joining it is the right move.

lines.text: Contemplating my own life. For the noble one, no mistake.
lines.meaning: The ruler’s line. Those in authority must judge themselves by the effect they have on others. If the people around you are thriving, your conduct is sound; if not, look first at yourself. You are watched and imitated, so examine your example carefully. Honest self-scrutiny of this kind keeps a leader free of blame.

lines.text: Contemplating their life. For the noble one, no mistake.
lines.meaning: At the top, beyond direct involvement, you look at life more broadly and from a distance, not just at your own ego but at what it means to live well. Freed from personal ambition, your view becomes wiser and others still look to you. Keep examining yourself even here, with humility. This detached, reflective stance brings no blame.

life.work: Survey the whole situation before you act, and lead through visible integrity rather than force.
life.love: Look more deeply at the other person than first impressions allow, and notice how your behavior affects them.
life.inner: Pause in quiet attention, like the moment before a ritual, and look honestly at your own life.

question: What would I see if I looked at this situation, and myself, without haste?

name: Biting Through
essence: Something is stuck between you and your goal, and it must be bitten through firmly. Clear judgment and real consequences restore order.

judgment.text: Biting through. Success. It is favorable to administer justice.
judgment.meaning: The hexagram looks like an open mouth, strong lines at top and bottom, with an obstacle lodged in it: the strong fourth line. The lips cannot close until the obstacle is bitten through. In life, something blocks union or progress: a deceiver, a dispute, a lie, a stubborn problem. It will not go away by itself. Energetic action is needed, and the outcome is good if you act. The trigrams show how: Thunder below brings force, Fire above brings clarity. Justice combines both. Find the facts, then apply fair and proportionate consequences, neither too soft nor too harsh. Do not let an unresolved wrong fester.

image.text: Thunder and lightning: the image of Biting Through. The ancient kings made penalties clear and the laws firm.
image.meaning: Lightning lights up the scene and thunder strikes with force. The wise ruler made the rules plain, so everyone could see them, and enforced them with consistency. The practice is to be clear about boundaries before trouble arises and to follow through when they are broken. Vague rules invite trouble; clear ones applied steadily keep the peace.

lines.text: His feet are locked in the stocks, and his toes disappear. No mistake.
lines.meaning: At the start, a light penalty for a first offense: like being put in the stocks for a short while. It stops someone before they go further. If you have made a small misstep and face a minor consequence, accept it; it keeps you from worse. If you must correct someone else, do it early and mildly. Caught now, the error does no lasting harm.

lines.text: Biting into tender meat, so deep the nose disappears. No mistake.
lines.meaning: It is easy to bite through what is soft, and you may bite too deep in your zeal. You are dealing with a clear case where you are in the right, and your reaction is perhaps stronger than needed. This is not a serious fault, since the cause is just. But notice when your firmness becomes excessive, and temper it.

lines.text: Biting into old dried meat, you hit something poisonous. Slight shame, but no mistake.
lines.meaning: The problem is old and tough, long left to harden, and when you take it on you meet resentment or ugly surprises. You may not have enough authority for the task, so people react with hostility. This causes some embarrassment. Still, the job needed doing, and you have not done wrong in tackling it. Carry on carefully.

lines.text: Biting into dried meat on the bone, you find metal arrowheads. It pays to stay aware of the difficulty and persevere. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: This is the hardest bite: the obstacle itself, gristle and bone with arrows lodged in it. Powerful resistance stands against you. The arrows suggest you must be as hard and straight as metal yourself. Do not underestimate the struggle, and do not give up. Persistent, clear-sighted effort will break through, and the outcome is good.

lines.text: Biting into dried lean meat, you find yellow gold. Stay true and aware of danger. No mistake.
lines.meaning: The case is hard but not impossible, and you are in a position to decide it. Yellow is the color of the center, of balance; gold is firm and true. You must be impartial and unwavering. You may be tempted to go easy because of your gentle nature, so be conscious of the risks of leniency. Steady, fair judgment brings no blame.

lines.text: His neck is locked in the wooden yoke, and his ears disappear. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: This is the hardened offender who did not listen to warnings and now bears the heaviest penalty: the yoke covers even his ears. If this describes you, you have ignored the signs for too long. If it describes someone else, they will not be reached by advice. This ends badly. Stop now and listen, before you are locked in by consequences.

life.work: Address the obstacle or conflict directly; get the facts clear and act with fair, proportionate firmness.
life.love: A hidden issue or a lie is blocking closeness; name it honestly so you can come together again.
life.inner: Do not hide from your own faults; small corrections now spare you heavy ones later.

question: What is lodged between me and what I want, and am I willing to bite through it?

name: Grace
essence: Grace is beauty and form: the elegance that makes life pleasant and ordered. It brings success in small things, but it is ornament, not substance.

judgment.text: Grace. Success. It is favorable to undertake small things.
judgment.meaning: Fire burns at the foot of the Mountain, lighting up its slopes and giving them color. That is grace: form, beauty, style, the polish and courtesy that make life lovely. It brings success, and it matters, since without form, relationships and work become crude. But the success is small. The light only reaches so far up the mountain. Ornament cannot replace substance or settle anything essential. So enjoy beauty, take care with presentation and manners, and attend to the details. Just do not mistake them for the core of the matter or expect them to carry big decisions.

image.text: Fire at the foot of the mountain: the image of Grace. The noble one brings clarity to ordinary affairs but does not dare to decide serious legal cases this way.
image.meaning: Firelight makes the mountain beautiful but does not illuminate it all. In the same way, a graceful and clear approach is enough to manage everyday matters well. Grave questions, however, those involving justice, conflict, or life’s big choices, need more than a pleasing surface. Use charm and good form for small things, and bring sober depth to serious ones.

lines.text: Giving grace to the toes. Leave the carriage and go on foot.
lines.meaning: At the beginning, the only adornment is to walk your own path humbly. You could accept an easy ride from someone that would not be quite right, but you choose to go on foot. Refuse help or comfort that comes with strings or compromises. Simple self-reliance at the start is its own grace, and it keeps your integrity intact.

lines.text: Giving grace to the beard.
lines.meaning: A beard has no life of its own; it moves only with the chin. Attention to appearance here is secondary, dependent on what lies beneath. You are fussing over a surface that only matters as an expression of something more real. Cultivate the substance, and let the beauty follow it. Vanity for its own sake is empty.

lines.text: Graceful and glistening. Lasting steadiness brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: Life is pleasant, attractive and smooth, like something glossy and moist. You enjoy being admired and well treated. The risk is sinking into comfort and losing your firmness. The line advises lasting steadiness: keep to your values even while things go well, and do not let charm dissolve your character. Then the good fortune endures.

lines.text: Grace or simplicity? A white horse comes as if on wings. Not a robber: he comes to woo.
lines.meaning: You are weighing elegance against plain sincerity, and simplicity wins. Someone approaches, perhaps in a way that at first seems intrusive or suspicious. But they are not a threat; they seek a genuine bond. Do not judge by appearance. Accept a sincere connection, even if it is less polished than you expected.

lines.text: Grace in the hills and gardens. The roll of silk is meager. Shame, but in the end good fortune.
lines.meaning: You withdraw from showy circles to seek something simpler and more real, perhaps a person or a life closer to nature. You have little to bring: your gift seems poor, and you may feel embarrassed. But what counts is the sincerity of your intention, not the size of the present. It works out well.

lines.text: Simple white grace. No mistake.
lines.meaning: At the end, all ornament falls away. The highest grace is pure simplicity, form so refined it no longer needs decoration, like plain white silk. Let your conduct and work speak plainly without embellishment. Remove what is superfluous. Nothing is lost by this, and it brings no blame.

life.work: Polish and presentation help with small matters; for major decisions rely on substance, not appearances.
life.love: Enjoy beauty and charm, but trust sincerity over polish and value what lies beneath the surface.
life.inner: Let your outer form express something real, and learn to prize simplicity.

question: Where am I relying on appearance when what is needed is substance?

name: Splitting Apart
essence: Splitting Apart is a time of decline, when the weak undermine the strong from below. Do not act against it; hold still, be generous, and protect the seed of what is good.

judgment.text: Splitting apart. It does not pay to go anywhere.
judgment.meaning: Five yielding lines rise from below and push the last strong line to the very top, about to fall. It is late autumn, when leaves drop and the structure gives way. Something you rely on is being eroded, a project, an institution, a relationship or your health, and the forces against it are in the ascendant. The omen is plain: undertaking anything now will not work. This is not cowardice; it is understanding the time. The trigrams advise stillness, Mountain above, on Earth that yields. Stay quiet, do not provoke, and wait. Decline runs its course, and the strength that remains at the top is the seed of renewal.

image.text: The mountain rests on the earth: the image of Splitting Apart. Those above secure their position by being generous to those below.
image.meaning: A mountain standing on narrow ground will crumble, but one resting on a broad base stays firm. In a time of erosion, what protects a position is not force but generosity to those below, who are its foundation. Take care of the people who support you, and broaden the base you stand on. That is what keeps a house from falling when the ground shakes.

lines.text: The legs of the bed are split. The steadfast are undone. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: The bed is where you rest, and its legs are being eaten away. Subversion begins at the base, quietly, through gossip, intrigue or small neglect. It strikes at those who are loyal and upright. There is little you can do directly now. Recognize what is happening, wait, and do not expose yourself. This stage goes badly.

lines.text: The frame of the bed is split. The steadfast are undone. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: The erosion has climbed higher and reached the frame. Danger is close, and you are isolated, with no help from those around you. Holding on stubbornly to your position will not work; it only puts you at risk. Be cautious, adapt, and avoid confrontation. You need patience to get through, since this phase too turns out badly.

lines.text: He splits with them. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Though you are surrounded by forces of decline, you keep a tie to the one strong line at the top, your correspondence. You break with the group you belong to in order to stay loyal to what is right. That may cost you friends or standing, but it is the right choice, and there is no blame in it.

lines.text: The bed is split up to the skin. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: Now the damage touches the person lying in the bed. The decline is no longer a threat; it is happening to you. There is no warning and no way to dodge the blow. All you can do is endure it and understand that it is the nature of this time, not a failure of yours. Misfortune.

lines.text: A string of fish. Through the women of the palace comes favor. Everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: The leader of the yielding lines now leads them, like fish strung together, to the strong line above, in loyalty, as a queen brings her ladies before the king. The forces of decline submit willingly to what is good. Things are reversed. When the weak accept the guidance of the strong, harmony returns. Everything goes well.

lines.text: A great fruit still uneaten. The noble one receives a carriage. The petty person’s house is split apart.
lines.meaning: At the top, a single strong line remains, like a large fruit left on the tree, whose seed will sprout again. Decline has run its course. The good person is now carried by others, given support and standing, while those who destroyed things end up destroying their own shelter. Keep the seed of your values safe. Renewal is close.

life.work: This is not the time to launch or fight; hold your position quietly, support those who support you, and wait.
life.love: Something is being worn down; avoid confrontation, be kind, and protect what is still good between you.
life.inner: Accept that decline is part of a cycle; keep the seed of your values and let the rest fall away.

question: What is the seed I need to protect while things fall apart?

name: Return
essence: After the darkest point, the light comes back. Return is the turning of the cycle and the recovery of your true path, a new beginning to be nurtured gently.

judgment.text: Return. Success. Going out and coming in without harm. Friends arrive, and there is no mistake. Back and forth goes the way. On the seventh day comes the return. It is favorable to have somewhere to go.
judgment.meaning: After Splitting Apart, a single strong line appears at the very bottom, beneath five yielding ones: the winter solstice, when the light starts to grow again. Return is a natural turn, not forced, so it happens without harm. Like-minded people gather, and it is fine. The way goes back and forth in its own rhythm; after seven stages, the return arrives. This is the time to come back to yourself, to your values and to what is good. The new movement is fragile, so do not rush. But do take a direction now. Having somewhere to go is favorable: the return should lead to forward motion.

image.text: Thunder within the earth: the image of Return. At the solstice the ancient kings closed the passes. Traders and travelers did not journey, and the ruler did not tour the realm.
image.meaning: Thunder resting inside the earth is energy just reawakening, still underground. At the solstice the ancient rulers gave everyone rest, so the returning life could gather strength. When you begin again after a hard time, protect the new start with quiet. Do not test it with too much activity or exposure. Rest, recover, and let it grow.

lines.text: Return from a short distance. No need for remorse. Great good fortune.
lines.meaning: You notice you have strayed from your path and turn back almost at once, before it goes too far. This is the best kind of return. No serious harm is done, and there is no reason for heavy regret. Correct the small error now, while it is easy. Catching yourself early and returning to what you know is right brings great good fortune.

lines.text: Quiet return. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: Return here is easy and calm, helped by a good example nearby: the strong first line just below. You do not have to struggle. It is enough to follow someone wise or to let yourself be drawn back to what is good. Lean on good company and gentle influence, and come back without fuss. Good fortune.

lines.text: Returning again and again. Danger, but no mistake.
lines.meaning: You keep wandering off and coming back: breaking resolutions, relapsing, starting over. That is unsettling and risky, since the habit of slipping can take hold. But each return is still a return, and it is better than not coming back at all. No blame. Aim for a steadier commitment, so you do not have to repeat the turn.

lines.text: Walking in the middle of others, you return alone.
lines.meaning: You are among people going one way, and you alone turn toward what is right. This line corresponds with the strong first line, the source of the return. Following your conscience may set you apart from the group. The text gives no omen, only the fact. You will be alone for a while, and that is the price of doing the right thing.

lines.text: Great-hearted return. No regret.
lines.meaning: In the place of the ruler, you face your faults openly and turn back nobly, with self-examination and without making excuses. It takes generosity of spirit to admit that you were wrong and change course. Doing it from the heart, with no evasion, leaves nothing to regret.

lines.text: Missing the return. Misfortune; disaster from within and without. If you send out armies, it ends in great defeat, and it brings misfortune on the ruler. For ten years no campaign can succeed.
lines.meaning: The moment to turn back was there and you missed it, by stubbornness or blindness. Now trouble comes both from your own mistakes and from outside. Pressing forward by force will lead to a serious collapse whose effects last a long time. This is the worst outcome of the hexagram. If you see yourself in it, stop and admit the mistake now, before it hardens.

life.work: A turn for the better is beginning; return to your core aim, set a direction, and build it gently without rushing.
life.love: Reconciliation is possible; come back sincerely, give it quiet and time, and do not force it.
life.inner: Notice when you have strayed and turn back early; the return to yourself is always available.

question: What do I need to return to, and how can I protect this new beginning?

name: Innocence
essence: Act from what is genuinely right rather than from calculation or design. When your intentions are clean, things go well; when you scheme or force, even good aims turn against you.

judgment.text: Innocence: great success, and it pays to stay true. Whoever is not as they should be meets misfortune, and it does not help them to set out on anything.
judgment.meaning: Wu Wang means “without falsehood” or “without expectation”. Thunder, the spark of movement, stirs beneath Heaven, the great order of things. Movement that springs from that order is natural and clean, and it succeeds without effort. The hexagram asks you to act from your truest instinct, not from a plan to get something. The warning is sharp: once you drift from what is right, or start working an angle, misfortune follows and nothing you undertake will prosper. Innocence here is not naivety. It is the alignment of your action with what the moment truly calls for. The name also hints at the unexpected: events may arrive that you did not plan for, good or bad. Meet them without manipulation. Check your motives, drop the hidden agenda, and let your conduct be simple and honest.

image.text: Beneath Heaven, thunder rolls, and every living thing is roused into its true nature. So the ancient kings, rich in virtue and attuned to the seasons, tended and nourished all beings.
image.meaning: Spring thunder wakes the world, and each seed grows into exactly what it is, without being told how. Wise leaders followed that example: they worked with the timing of things and cared for others according to their nature, rather than imposing a scheme. For you, the practice is to notice what season you are in and respond to it fully, supporting growth in yourself and others instead of bending it to your design.

lines.text: Going forward in innocence brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: A firm yang line at the very start, the first stirring of thunder. Your first impulse here is sound. You do not need to second-guess it or dress it up with strategy. Move with a clear heart and a straightforward purpose, and things will go well. The danger would be in overthinking, not in acting. Trust the simple, honest step in front of you.

lines.text: Do not plow with the harvest in mind, nor clear new ground counting on the rich field it will become. Then it is good to go forward.
lines.meaning: This yin line sits in the centre and corresponds with the ruler above, so it can act well, but only if it lets go of calculating returns. Do the work because it is the work that needs doing. When every task is a means to a payoff, you grow anxious and distorted. Give each stage your full attention for its own sake, and the results will take care of themselves. Then you can proceed.

lines.text: Undeserved misfortune. Someone tied up a cow; a passing traveler takes it, and the villagers nearby get the blame.
lines.meaning: Trouble can land on you that you did nothing to cause. The traveler gains, the people who happened to be close by suffer suspicion and loss. This line is a reminder that innocence does not guarantee immunity. Do not torment yourself looking for your own fault, and do not let the injustice make you bitter or crooked. Accept that this is how the world sometimes works, protect what you can, and keep your conduct clean.

lines.text: If you can stay steady and true, there is no mistake.
lines.meaning: A firm line in a yielding place, close to the ruler, with no partner below to lean on. You cannot be pulled off course by others, and you should not try to recruit them either. Hold to what you know is right, quietly and by yourself. This is not a time for big moves but for constancy. What is truly yours cannot be taken away, so you need not grasp for anything.

lines.text: An illness you did nothing to bring on: do not reach for medicine. It will pass, and there will be joy.
lines.meaning: The ruler is strong, central and correct, yet trouble appears anyway. Because it does not come from any error of yours, it does not need a drastic cure. Forcing a remedy, rushing to fix, or changing course in alarm could create a real problem where there was only a passing one. Stay calm and let the disturbance run its course. Patience is the right treatment, and relief will come.

lines.text: Acting now, even in innocence, brings misfortune. Nothing is gained by it.
lines.meaning: At the end of the hexagram, the time for movement has run out. Even honest, well-meant action will not land, because the moment has passed. Pushing on regardless turns innocence into stubbornness. Recognize that a natural cycle has closed. Rest, observe, and wait for a new beginning instead of insisting on one more push.

life.work: Do the task well for its own sake and drop the hidden angles; schemes will backfire, while plain good work will be noticed.
life.love: Be sincere, without strategy or games, and do not treat affection as a transaction with an expected return.
life.inner: Practice catching the moment when you start calculating, and return to what you would do if no one were keeping score.

question: What would I do here if I expected nothing in return?

name: Great Taming
essence: Great energy is being held, gathered and trained rather than spent. Restraint now builds a reserve of strength, knowledge and character that you will later use for something large.

judgment.text: Great Taming: it pays to stay the course. Not eating at home brings good fortune. It is favorable to cross the great river.
judgment.meaning: The three strong lines of Heaven are held back by the Mountain above them. That restraint is not defeat; it is how great power gets stored, focused and trained. The hexagram has three parts. Hold firm and steady, because strength without discipline is wasted. “Not eating at home” means taking your place in wider life, serving and being supported publicly instead of retreating into private comfort; capable people should be employed, not idle. And the great river can be crossed: with energy well gathered, you are ready for a serious undertaking. Keep renewing yourself each day, as the commentary says, so that what you hold does not go stale. Restraint here is the preparation of a large force.

image.text: Heaven is held within the mountain. So the noble one learns many words of the ancients and deeds of the past, and so strengthens their character.
image.meaning: A mountain containing the sky is an image of enormous treasure stored in a small space. The way you do this in yourself is by study: absorbing what wise people have said and done before you. Knowledge of the past is not mere information; digested, it becomes judgment and character. This is a good time to read, learn from experience, and let what you learn shape how you act.

lines.text: Danger is near. It is better to stop.
lines.meaning: Your strength wants to charge ahead, but the line corresponding to you above is the very force that holds you back. Pushing now would mean collision. This is not failure of nerve; it is good sense. Halt, gather yourself, and let the moment ripen. Restraint at the very start saves you from a damaging clash.

lines.text: The axle-block is taken out of the cart.
lines.meaning: Here the brake is applied from within. You see that movement is blocked and you voluntarily take your cart off the road. Because the line is central, it knows the measure of things and feels no resentment. Do not strain against the obstacle. Pause your plans, repair and prepare, and trust that the waiting is productive.

lines.text: Good horses run together. It pays to know the hardship and stay firm. Drill every day with chariot and defense. It is good to have somewhere to go.
lines.meaning: The way is opening and you can move forward alongside a strong ally, the top line, which no longer blocks you. But freedom is not license. Stay aware of danger, keep your discipline, and practice your skills daily so you are ready for what lies ahead. Progress made with care and preparation goes well. Racing ahead carelessly would undo it.

lines.text: A guard-board on the horns of a young bull. Great good fortune.
lines.meaning: Before a young bull’s horns grow dangerous, a board is fixed over them. The wise way to tame a strong force is early and gently, before it gets out of hand. Whether the force is in someone else, in a situation, or in your own temper, step in at the beginning with a simple measure. This saves conflict later, and it brings real good fortune.

lines.text: The tusks of a gelded boar. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: The boar’s tusks are dangerous, but attacking the tusks directly is hopeless. Change the animal’s nature at its root and the tusks stop being a threat. The ruler deals with wild energy by addressing its source, not its symptoms. In your situation, look beneath the aggression, craving or chaos for what drives it, and work there. Indirect and fundamental beats forceful and frontal.

lines.text: What a highway of Heaven. Success.
lines.meaning: The long restraint is over. The stored strength is released and the way lies open, broad as the sky. Everything you gathered and trained now flows outward freely. This is the reward of disciplined preparation: action that is unobstructed and aligned. Move confidently. The time of holding back has fulfilled its purpose.

life.work: Build skill, savings and knowledge now; hold back from premature launches, and when the way clears, step into a public role and take on the big project.
life.love: Contain impulses and strong feelings without suppressing them; steady restraint makes a relationship trustworthy and deep.
life.inner: Study and reflect daily, turning what you learn into character rather than letting energy leak away in restlessness.

question: What strength am I gathering, and what am I gathering it for?

name: Nourishment
essence: Pay attention to what feeds you and how you feed others. Body, mind and character are all shaped by what you take in and what you give out.

judgment.text: Nourishment: staying true brings good fortune. Watch how nourishment is given, and what a person seeks to fill their own mouth with.
judgment.meaning: The hexagram is a picture of an open mouth: firm lines top and bottom like jaws, broken lines between. Mountain above is still, Thunder below moves, as the upper jaw holds while the lower chews. The question is what you nourish and how. Look at two things: whom and what you care for, and what you crave for yourself. You can judge anyone, yourself included, by these. Good fortune comes from nourishing in the right way: the body with moderate food, the mind with good ideas, the character with worthy aims, and others with real support rather than flattery or indulgence. Feeding on the wrong things, or depending on the wrong people, gradually ruins you. Choose carefully what goes into your mouth and what comes out of it.

image.text: Thunder at the foot of the mountain. So the noble one is careful in speech and moderate in eating and drinking.
image.meaning: Movement stirs below while the mountain stays still, like the jaw working under a calm face. The mouth is where food goes in and words come out, so both deserve care. Speak with thought, because words shape what others take in. Eat and drink with moderation, because excess dulls body and judgment. The practice is simple but demanding: guard the gate of the mouth in both directions.

lines.text: You let your magic tortoise go, and stare at me with your jaw hanging. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: The tortoise, which can live without eating, stands for inner self-sufficiency. A strong line at the bottom has its own resources, yet it gapes enviously at what others have. Giving up your own independence to covet someone else’s food, wealth or status goes badly. You already have what you need to sustain yourself. Stop comparing, return to your own sources, and you regain your dignity.

lines.text: Turning upside down for nourishment, straying from the proper path to seek it from the hill. Pressing on brings misfortune.
lines.meaning: Instead of providing for yourself, or seeking support where it naturally belongs, you look for handouts from someone above who has no reason to give them. This is unnatural and it erodes self-respect. Continuing this way leads to trouble. Look for honest means of support. Stand on your own feet, or ask from the proper source, not from whoever seems easiest to lean on.

lines.text: Turning away from true nourishment. Persisting brings misfortune. Do not act this way for ten years. Nothing is gained.
lines.meaning: This line chases what gratifies rather than what feeds: one pleasure after another, never satisfied. It is the line of craving, and it leads nowhere good. The text is unusually strong: the damage could last a long time. If you see yourself here, recognize the pattern and step out of it. Real nourishment satisfies; compulsive consumption only leaves you emptier.

lines.text: Turning upside down for nourishment brings good fortune. Watching like a tiger, with an unending hunger. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Seeking support from below is ordinarily a reversal, but here it is right. This yin line near the ruler cannot do its task alone, so it looks to the strong line at the bottom for capable help. Search for good people and resources with the focus of a hungry tiger. Because the hunger is for the means to serve others, not for personal gain, there is no fault in it.

lines.text: Turning from the usual path. Staying firm and still brings good fortune. Do not cross the great river.
lines.meaning: The ruler here is a yielding line, not strong enough to nourish everyone alone. It departs from the normal order by leaning on the wise strength of the top line. That is fine as long as you are steady and quiet. Accept guidance, keep your position, and do not attempt big ventures that require more strength than you have. This is a time to be supported, not to lead a crossing.

lines.text: The source of nourishment. Aware of the danger, you find good fortune. It is favorable to cross the great river.
lines.meaning: The strong top line is the one through whom everyone is fed. This is a heavy responsibility. If you stay aware of its weight and the risks of misusing it, good fortune follows. Being so central to others gives you the standing to undertake something large for their benefit. Carry it seriously and generously, and the great undertaking will succeed.

life.work: Notice what really sustains your work and whom you depend on; support others with substance, and be wary of easy dependence or flattery.
life.love: Care for the people close to you with what genuinely helps them, and watch both what you say and what you demand.
life.inner: Audit your inputs, from food to media to company, and keep what truly nourishes; speak less and more carefully.

question: What am I feeding on, and what am I feeding others?

name: Great Exceeding
essence: Too much weight rests on too weak a structure, and the situation is near the breaking point. It calls for extraordinary action, taken with care, and the courage to stand alone if necessary.

judgment.text: Great Exceeding: the ridgepole sags. It is favorable to have somewhere to go. Success.
judgment.meaning: Four strong lines crowd the middle while the two ends are weak, like a roof beam heavy at the centre and frail where it rests. The ridgepole bends; collapse is possible. This is an exceptional time, and ordinary methods will not do. Yet the omen is not doom. It is favorable to act and move, and success is possible, because the strong lines at the centre have the power to respond. The trigrams show how: Wind below means gentleness and penetration, Lake above means joy. Do not panic or force a violent fix. Find a way out, gently but decisively, and do not wait for the beam to snap. Great times demand that you go beyond the usual, and do it with care.

image.text: The lake rises over the trees. So the noble one, standing alone, is not afraid, and withdrawing from the world, is not dismayed.
image.meaning: When the water climbs above the trees, it is a flood, an extraordinary event. In such times you may find yourself in a minority of one, or needing to step away from the crowd altogether. The noble one stays calm in both cases. Take your stand on what you know is right, without needing approval, and if you must retreat, do it without bitterness or fear. Inner steadiness is what lets you endure exceptional pressure.

lines.text: Spread white rushes underneath. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Before setting something heavy down, you lay a mat of clean white rushes to protect it. In a delicate, overloaded situation, extreme care at the start is exactly right. It may look like excessive caution, but here caution is wisdom. Prepare the ground, treat what you handle with respect, and you will avoid mistakes.

lines.text: A withered willow puts out new shoots from its root. An older man takes a young wife. Everything goes well.
lines.meaning: A strong line low and central, close to the yielding bottom line, joins with something young and fresh. Renewal comes from an unusual pairing: experience allied with new energy, an old structure grafted with new life. In an overstrained situation, this kind of unexpected combination is what revives things. Reach out to what is humbler or newer than you. It brings good results in every direction.

lines.text: The ridgepole sags. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: A strong line in a strong place, it insists on its own way and accepts no support. Pressing forward with force, ignoring advice and the signs of strain, brings the beam down. If you are carrying everything yourself and refusing help, you are heading for a break. Ease off, listen, and let others share the load before it is too late.

lines.text: The ridgepole is braced. Good fortune. If you have other motives, there will be shame.
lines.meaning: Here the strength is tempered by a yielding position, so the beam holds. You are able to steady the situation and support those who rely on you. Good fortune. But the warning is plain: if you use this position for selfish ends, or lean toward the weak line below for personal gain, you will be humiliated. Stay with the larger purpose.

lines.text: A withered willow bursts into flower. An older woman takes a young husband. No blame, and no praise.
lines.meaning: Blossom on a dead tree is beautiful, but it uses up the last strength instead of producing new growth. The ruler joins with the weak top line, which offers nothing to renew it. The effort is not wrong, but it does not lead anywhere lasting. Be honest about whether a move merely decorates a tired situation or truly revives it. Look for something with roots.

lines.text: Wading through the water, it closes over your head. Misfortune. No blame.
lines.meaning: You walk into danger to accomplish something and are overwhelmed. The outcome is bad. But because the aim was right, no one can fault you. There are times when the right thing costs you dearly. The line does not promise rescue; it honors the choice. If you face this, know that integrity is not the same as success, and both are worth weighing clearly.

life.work: You are over capacity and something must change; act soon and creatively, share the load, and avoid both panic and brute force.
life.love: A relationship under strain needs care and fresh thinking, not pressure; unusual solutions may serve better than conventional ones.
life.inner: Find the steadiness to stand alone in what you believe without fear, and the humility to accept help before you break.

question: Where am I carrying more than the structure can bear, and what would relieve it?

name: The Abyss
essence: You are in danger upon danger, like water in a ravine. The way through is to keep your heart sincere and to move as water does: steadily, without losing its nature.

judgment.text: The Abyss, doubled. If you are sincere, your heart finds its way through, and action is worth taking and brings honor.
judgment.meaning: Water above water: one gorge leads into another. Each trigram is a strong line trapped between two weak ones, an image of something true enclosed by peril. This is a time of real and repeated danger, and the hexagram does not play it down. What it offers is a method. Water does not stop at a drop or fear a gorge; it fills each hollow and flows on, always remaining water. Hold to your inner truth in the same way. If you are sincere and your mind stays clear, you can pass through. Act; do not freeze in the pit. Repeated danger also trains you: by meeting it without losing yourself, you become someone who can be trusted with difficulty.

image.text: Water flows on and on and reaches its goal. So the noble one keeps virtue constant and practices the work of teaching.
image.meaning: Water arrives by not stopping. It keeps flowing, filling every low place before moving on. Character is built the same way: by steady, repeated practice, not by single efforts. Teaching works like this too, through patient repetition until something is truly learned. When you are in difficulty, keep doing the right things consistently. Constancy carries you, and others, through.

lines.text: The abyss doubled. In the abyss, you fall into a pit within it. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: A weak line at the very bottom of danger, with nothing to hold onto. You have become so used to difficulty that you sink further into it, perhaps by habit or by losing your sense of direction. This goes badly. Recognize that you have slipped from danger into a deeper hole. Stop digging, seek solid ground, and do not normalize the bad situation.

lines.text: The abyss is dangerous. Seek only small gains.
lines.meaning: A strong line at the centre of the lower danger: capable, but still surrounded. You cannot escape all at once. Aim for small, achievable steps rather than a grand rescue. Each small success keeps you afloat and gives you footing for the next. Patience and modest aims are the right strategy here.

lines.text: Coming and going, pit after pit. Danger here, and nothing to lean on. You only sink deeper. Do not act this way.
lines.meaning: Caught between two stretches of danger, every move seems to lead to another hole. Restless action only makes things worse. The line advises stillness: stop thrashing, wait, and observe. When you cannot see a way forward, the best action is to do nothing reckless and let a real opening appear.

lines.text: A jug of wine, a bowl of rice besides, in plain clay vessels, passed in through the window. In the end, no mistake.
lines.meaning: In danger, formality falls away. A simple offering is passed through a window rather than the front door; an honest gesture between this minister and the ruler above, who are close and need each other. Approach people plainly and sincerely, without ceremony or pretense. Simple truth and genuine help, offered in whatever way is possible, will be received. In the end, no fault.

lines.text: The abyss does not overflow. It fills only to the level. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Water filling a pit does not rise above its rim; it simply levels off and then flows out. The ruler, strong and central, is near the end of danger. Do not try to do more than is needed. Get through this by doing just enough, along the line of least resistance. Excess ambition now would reopen the danger. Measured effort brings you out.

lines.text: Bound with cords and ropes, shut in among thorn hedges. For three years you do not find the way. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: A weak line at the very top, having strayed too far, is caught as if in prison. This is the result of losing the way in danger: trapped by your own mistakes or by circumstances you misjudged. The time of confinement is long. Accept it honestly, learn from it, and do not compound it with further errors. Release comes only after a long reckoning.

life.work: Expect difficulty to continue for a while; aim for small, steady progress, keep your integrity, and do not freeze or panic.
life.love: In hard times, plain honesty and simple gestures of care matter far more than grand words.
life.inner: Hold to your inner truth like water holds its nature, flowing through each trouble without becoming it.

question: What is the true thing in me that can flow through this danger unchanged?

name: The Clinging
essence: Fire gives light only by clinging to something that burns. Clarity and brightness depend on what you attach yourself to, so attach to what is right and tend it with gentle care.

judgment.text: The Clinging: staying true is favorable, and brings success. Caring for the cow brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: Fire has no shape of its own; it exists by clinging to wood. Each trigram is a weak line held between two strong ones, an empty, clear centre, like the hollow of a flame. Light and understanding work the same way: they rely on something to hold onto. So the essential question is what you cling to. Choose what is right and steady, and your clarity will last. The cow, gentle and patient, is the image of the right attitude: humble, docile, receptive. Tend that quality in yourself. Brilliance that is proud or grasping burns out; brilliance founded on gentle acceptance and devotion to what is good brings success and real illumination for others.

image.text: Brightness rises twice, forming Fire. So the great person, carrying this light forward, lights up the four corners of the world.
image.meaning: One sun follows another, day after day. The doubled fire is clarity sustained over time. A great person does not shine once; they keep renewing their understanding and let it spread outward, so that their light illuminates everyone around them. The practice is to keep your own mind clear consistently, and to share understanding generously rather than hoarding it.

lines.text: Footsteps crisscross in confusion. If you treat this with respect and care, there is no mistake.
lines.meaning: Early morning, the day is starting and everything rushes in at once. Impressions, tasks and demands cross each other. If you plunge in hastily, you will scatter yourself. Instead, begin with seriousness and attention. Collect yourself at the outset, because the first steps set the direction of the whole day, or the whole project. Done that way, no mistake.

lines.text: Yellow light. Supreme good fortune.
lines.meaning: Yellow is the colour of the centre and of the middle way. This yielding line sits in the heart of the lower fire, the gentle light of midday, neither glaring nor faint. Clarity based on moderation and balance is the best possible kind. Keep to the centre, avoid extremes, and your understanding will be both warm and true. This is one of the most fortunate lines in the book.

lines.text: In the light of the setting sun, people either drum on pots and sing, or groan and wail at old age. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: The lower fire is ending, and with it a stage of life. Faced with the fact that all things pass, people swing between reckless merriment and despair. Both are failures of balance. The misfortune is in losing your composure about impermanence. Accept the evening calmly. Neither forced cheerfulness nor lament helps; equanimity does.

lines.text: It comes suddenly. It flares up, it dies down, it is thrown away.
lines.meaning: A strong line pushes abruptly upward against the ruler, like a fire that blazes up and burns out. Sudden brilliance without a real fuel source does not last; it consumes itself and is cast off. Be wary of meteoric success or headlong ambition, in yourself or others. Lasting light needs steady fuel and a proper place. Slow down and root yourself.

lines.text: Tears in floods, sighing and grieving. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: The ruler is a yielding line pressed between strong ones, in a hard place. But it responds with genuine sorrow and deep awareness of its situation, not with pride. That heartfelt seriousness is what turns things around. Real change of heart, even when it hurts, brings good fortune. Let yourself feel the weight of things fully, and let it change you.

lines.text: The king sends him out to set things right. He does well: he strikes down the ringleaders and spares those who merely followed. No mistake.
lines.meaning: At the top, clarity becomes the power to judge and correct. When disorder must be dealt with, deal with its roots, the chief sources of the problem, and be lenient with those who were only carried along. Discipline should be clear-sighted, not wholesale. In your own life, eliminate the core bad habits and do not punish yourself for every minor fault. No mistake.

life.work: Attach yourself to a worthy cause, mentor or principle, bring clear understanding to your work, and avoid flashy bursts that burn out.
life.love: Healthy dependence is natural; cling to what is good for you, tend it gently, and let each bring light to the other.
life.inner: Cultivate a calm, receptive clarity and stay centered, neither elated nor despairing as things rise and pass.

question: What am I clinging to, and does it make my light clearer or burn me out?

name: Influence
essence: Two forces are drawn to each other and respond. True influence comes from openness and stillness, not pressure, and it is the basis of attraction, friendship and partnership.

judgment.text: Influence: success. It pays to stay true. Taking a wife brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: The Lake, the youngest daughter, rests above; the Mountain, the youngest son, is below and yields to her. The strong one humbles itself before the gentle one, and the two attract and respond. This is the force of courtship, of mutual feeling, and more broadly of all real influence: one heart moves another. The Chinese character for feeling is xian with the heart added; here the heart is implied. Influence succeeds when it is sincere and correct, not manipulative. Stillness within, joy without: you are steady and calm, and therefore open. Commitment, symbolized by marriage, brings good fortune. Whether in love, friendship or leadership, influence that comes from genuine openness lasts; pressure and charm only seduce.

image.text: A lake rests on the mountain. So the noble one receives others with an open, empty mind.
image.meaning: The mountaintop holds a hollow, and the lake gathers there, feeding the mountain with moisture. To be influenced and to influence, you must have room in you. A mind already full of opinions, pride and agendas cannot receive anything. Make space: listen, stay humble, be open to others. People are drawn to someone who genuinely receives them.

lines.text: The influence shows in the big toe.
lines.meaning: Something has begun to move you, but it is only at the edge, barely visible. Like a twitch in the toe, an intention is forming before the body moves. It is too early to tell where it leads, and no omen is given. Notice the stirring, but do not act on it yet. Let it become clearer.

lines.text: The influence shows in the calves. Misfortune. Staying put brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: The calves move when the body walks, but they cannot choose the direction themselves. You feel impelled to act, to follow, before the situation is ready. This goes badly. Wait, be still, and let a proper response come from a deeper place. Acting on impulse here would bring trouble.

lines.text: The influence shows in the thighs. You hold to what you follow. Going on this way brings regret.
lines.meaning: The thighs move only when the feet move; they follow without discernment. You are letting yourself be carried along by others’ wishes or by every passing desire. Persisting in this leads to humiliation. Find your own centre and act from it, rather than giving in to whatever pulls at you.

lines.text: Staying true brings good fortune, and regret vanishes. If your mind is restless, thoughts going back and forth, only your close friends will follow your thoughts.
lines.meaning: This is the place of the heart, and the line has no body part: it is the source of true influence. When your heart is steady and correct, your influence works naturally and regret disappears. But if you scheme and fret, trying to manage how others think of you, your effect shrinks to a small circle of people who already agree with you. Settle the mind, and let sincerity do the work.

lines.text: The influence shows in the back of the neck. No regret.
lines.meaning: The back of the neck is the stiffest part of the body, the least moved by feeling. The ruler here is firm and unmoved, which keeps it from being swept away, so there is nothing to regret. But it also means it does not truly influence anyone. Steadiness is good. Make sure it does not become coldness or detachment.

lines.text: The influence shows in the jaws, cheeks and tongue.
lines.meaning: At the top, influence has become only talk. Words without a heart behind them move no one deeply. The text gives no omen, but the image speaks for itself: smooth persuasion, flattery and chatter are the shallowest kind of influence. If you want to move people, let your actions and sincerity speak, not just your mouth.

life.work: Influence colleagues by being open and receptive, not pushy; respond to people, and lead by sincerity rather than salesmanship.
life.love: Mutual attraction is strong and favorable; let it build honestly, with humility and commitment, rather than chasing or rushing.
life.inner: Empty yourself of fixed opinions so you can truly receive others, and keep your heart steady at the centre.

question: Where can I make room in myself so that I can truly be moved, and move others?

name: Duration
essence: What lasts is not rigid but self-renewing, like the cycle of the seasons. Duration means holding a steady direction through change, keeping to your course and your commitments.

judgment.text: Duration: success, no mistake. It pays to stay the course. It is favorable to have somewhere to go.
judgment.meaning: Thunder above, Wind below: the eldest son and eldest daughter, the image of a settled marriage, where the strong leads outwardly and the gentle supports within. Thunder and wind always come together and keep moving, yet their relationship stays the same. That is the nature of duration. It is not standstill but constancy in motion, like the sun and moon that keep shining because they follow their course, or the seasons that last by changing. The omen is good: success, no blame, as long as you persevere in what is right and keep a direction. Endurance comes from commitment to a purpose, renewed day by day, not from clinging to things as they are.

image.text: Thunder and wind together. So the noble one stands firm and does not change direction.
image.meaning: Thunder and wind are the most mobile things in nature, yet they always accompany each other. Amid all movement, the noble one has an inner direction that does not waver. You can adapt your methods to circumstances, bend with the times, and still keep your basic course. Constancy of aim, not inflexibility of means, is what makes something last.

lines.text: Seeking duration too deeply, too soon. Staying this course brings misfortune. Nothing is gained.
lines.meaning: At the very start you demand permanence at once, digging deep before the foundations are laid. This is impatience disguised as commitment. Lasting things grow gradually. Wanting everything settled immediately, in work or in love, leads to disappointment. Slow down, let trust and understanding build, and do not demand guarantees at the beginning.

lines.text: Regret vanishes.
lines.meaning: A strong line in a yielding place, which might be a source of regret. But it is central, so it knows how to keep to the middle and not overreach. By staying within the limits of what you can actually sustain, you avoid excess. Regret disappears because you are steady rather than ambitious. Keep a measured pace.

lines.text: Not keeping your character steady, you meet with disgrace. Persisting brings regret.
lines.meaning: This line is restless, swinging between moods and impressions, at the mercy of every outside influence. Without inner constancy, your actions become unpredictable and people lose trust in you, which brings shame. If you go on this way, you will regret it. Find what you stand for and hold to it.

lines.text: No game in the field.
lines.meaning: You are hunting persistently, but in the wrong place: there is nothing to catch here. Perseverance alone does not guarantee results if you are aiming at the wrong goal or working in the wrong setting. Stop and reconsider. Steadiness is only valuable when it is directed rightly. Change your field, not your effort.

lines.text: Holding your character steady and true. For a wife, good fortune; for a husband, misfortune.
lines.meaning: The ruler here is yielding and faithfully follows its partner below. Traditionally, loyal following was the right constancy for one in a supporting role, but leaders must act according to what each situation requires rather than simply adhering. Read it broadly: steady loyalty is right when your role is to support; when your role is to lead and decide, mere adherence to habit or to others goes badly. Know which role you are in.

lines.text: Restlessness as a lasting state. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: At the end of duration, constancy has turned into constant agitation. Always busy, always changing, never at rest, you wear out yourself and those around you. This goes badly. The deeper calm needed for lasting achievement is lost in perpetual motion. Stop rushing, let things settle, and find again the quiet centre from which steady action flows.

life.work: Commit to a long-term direction and work at it steadily; adapt your methods without abandoning your aim.
life.love: Lasting love grows gradually and is renewed day by day; keep faith, and do not demand permanence too soon.
life.inner: Build an inner constancy that survives changing moods, and make sure your persistence is aimed in the right direction.

question: What in my life deserves steady commitment, and am I aiming my persistence well?

name: Retreat
essence: A force you cannot stop is on the rise, and the wise move is to step back in good order. Retreat here is not defeat; it is how you keep your strength intact for a better day.

judgment.text: Retreat. There is success in it. In small matters, staying steady is still to your advantage.
judgment.meaning: Look at the figure: two broken lines are climbing up from below, pushing the four solid lines upward and out. The dark, petty or hostile element is growing, and it is not yet time to fight it head on. To keep pressing would only use you up. So the success promised here comes through withdrawal, done at the right moment and with your dignity whole. Retreating is an active choice, not a collapse: you pull back from a position you can no longer hold, so that you are not dragged down with it. Big ventures are not favored now. Small, careful steps and quiet persistence still work. Leave before you are pushed, and leave without bitterness.

image.text: Mountain beneath Heaven: the image of Retreat. The noble one keeps small-minded people at a distance, not with anger but with a calm and unbending reserve.
image.meaning: The mountain rises toward the sky, yet the sky draws back from it and stays out of reach. That is the stance to take toward people or forces that would drag you into pettiness. You do not need to hate them, quarrel with them, or prove a point. You simply do not let them close. Firm boundaries, held politely, keep you clear without making you a new enemy.

lines.text: Retreating at the tail. Dangerous. Do not try to go anywhere now.
lines.meaning: You are at the back of the column, the last to leave, and the trouble is right behind you. This is a risky place, and any bold move will draw attention. Do not start something new or try to break away dramatically. Keep still, keep a low profile, and wait for the danger to pass you by. Quiet stillness is safer here than a late, hurried escape.

lines.text: He is bound fast with the hide of a yellow ox. No one can work it loose.
lines.meaning: Yellow is the color of the center and of loyalty; oxhide is the toughest of bindings. In a time when others are leaving, you hold firmly to what is right, or to the person of worth you are attached to. Nothing can pull you away. Your steadiness may be what lets a better person withdraw safely. Commitment, here, is a strength: hold your ground in your conviction even while the outer situation shifts.

lines.text: A retreat that is held back. Sickness and danger. Keeping servants and maids around you brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: You know you should leave, but ties hold you: obligations, people who depend on you, things you cannot simply drop. This half-retreat is wearing and dangerous, like an illness that lingers. Since you cannot go cleanly, make the best of it. Keep people who rely on you close, but treat these as practical ties, not as the place where your real work or loyalty lies. That handles the moment. Do not try anything great from here.

lines.text: A willing retreat. Good fortune for the noble one; ruin for the petty.
lines.meaning: You still feel drawn to what you are leaving, and the line below you pulls at you. But you can let go freely, without resentment, because you see that the time has turned. For a person of character this is a clean, good departure. For someone who cannot let go, the same moment brings ruin, because they cling and are swept away. The difference is your inner freedom. Go while you still can.

lines.text: An admirable retreat, well timed. Staying the course brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are in the center of the upper trigram, in a strong position, and you withdraw at exactly the right moment, gracefully and without fuss. Because you are decisive, nobody can talk you out of it, and because you are courteous, nobody takes offense. Hold to your decision firmly. People may try to delay you with friendly arguments; do not let them. This kind of retreat earns respect and keeps the future open.

lines.text: A carefree retreat, far and free. Everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: You are at the top, beyond the struggle, with no ties holding you back. You withdraw with a light heart, without doubt and without looking back. Because you are not entangled, nothing can follow you or harm you. This is the best kind of leaving: complete, cheerful and sure. Whatever you turn to next opens before you. Let go fully and enjoy the freedom it gives.

life.work: Step back from a losing fight, a declining project or a toxic dynamic before it costs you more; protect your energy and reputation for the next real opening.
life.love: Create distance from someone who keeps drawing you into conflict, calmly and without blame, rather than fighting a battle that cannot be won.
life.inner: Practice detachment: withdraw your attention from petty provocations and keep your center intact.

question: What am I holding on to that it is already time to leave, and how can I go with my dignity whole?

name: Great Power
essence: Your strength is high and rising. The test is not whether you have power but whether you use it rightly, with restraint and in line with what is fair.

judgment.text: Great Power. Staying true to what is right is to your advantage.
judgment.meaning: Four solid lines push up from below, and the strength has passed the center of the figure. Thunder moves above Heaven: energy is surging, things are going your way, and you feel able to do almost anything. That is exactly the danger. Power that rests only on itself becomes forceful, careless and blind to others, and then it breaks against something. The text gives just one counsel: hold to what is right. Real greatness of power lies in being joined to fairness and good sense. Use the moment, but do not let the feeling of strength lead you to push, bully or overreach. When you can wait, you are strong; when you must force, you are not.
