image.text: Thunder high above Heaven: the image of Great Power. The noble one does not set foot on any path that does not accord with what is proper.
image.meaning: Thunder rolling up through the whole sky is power at its most impressive. The truly strong person turns this power inward, toward self-mastery. To refuse any step that is not right takes more strength than pushing ahead does. So the practice is discipline: let your conduct, not your force, be what is great. Mastering your own impulses is the deepest use of power.

lines.text: Power in the toes. Pushing forward brings misfortune. That is certain.
lines.meaning: You are at the very bottom, eager to move, with all the strength gathered in your feet but no standing yet. If you charge ahead now, it will go badly; there is no doubt about it. You have the energy but not the position, the support or the timing. Hold it. Let the strength settle and gather, and wait for a moment when your movement will carry real weight.

lines.text: Staying steady brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: A strong line in a yielding, central place. Things are beginning to open, and resistance is giving way. This is where many get overconfident. Instead, keep to the middle path: moderate, balanced, persistent. Do not let early success push you into excess. If you stay steady and do not overplay your hand, things go well. The line’s good fortune comes precisely from its restraint.

lines.text: The small-minded use force; the noble one does not. Persisting is dangerous. A ram butts a hedge and gets its horns caught.
lines.meaning: At the restless top of the lower trigram, strength wants to prove itself. A crude person pushes; a wise person, even when strong, holds back. If you insist on battering through, you will be like the ram whose horns are stuck in a thorny hedge, unable to move forward or pull free. Brute force here traps you. Back off, use less, and find another way.

lines.text: Staying steady brings good fortune, and regret fades. The hedge opens and nothing holds you. Power lies in the axle of a great cart.
lines.meaning: Now the obstacle gives way, not because you rammed it but because you persisted quietly. A big cart is strong because of its axle, which is hidden and bears the load. Your strength is like that: it works best when it is not shown off. Keep going steadily, without bluster, and the way clears. Earlier doubts and regrets fall away as the obstacle dissolves.

lines.text: He loses the ram with ease. No regret.
lines.meaning: The ram is the stubborn, butting spirit. You are in the ruler’s place, but this line is yielding, so you can simply let that combative attitude go, easily, as though letting an animal wander off. There is nothing left to fight about, and no need to keep proving how strong you are. Dropping the urge to push leaves you with no regret. Gentle authority is enough here.

lines.text: A ram butts a hedge. It can go neither back nor forward. Nothing is favorable. If you see the difficulty, good fortune follows.
lines.meaning: You have pushed too far and now you are stuck, unable to advance and unable to retreat. Nothing works from here by more force. But the line holds out a way out: once you clearly see and admit how stuck you are, you can calm down, stop struggling and let things change. Accepting the difficulty is the beginning of release. The good fortune comes after you stop butting.

life.work: You have momentum and leverage; use them for something right and lasting, and avoid forcing outcomes or steamrolling colleagues.
life.love: Strength in a relationship shows as restraint and fairness, not as winning every argument.
life.inner: Ask whether your energy is serving your values or just your will; let self-mastery be your real power.

question: Where am I pushing simply because I can, and what would it look like to use my strength rightly?

name: Progress
essence: Like the sun climbing over the earth, things are moving upward easily and you are being seen. Progress comes from bright, generous conduct and from serving something larger.

judgment.text: Progress. The prince who brings peace is honored with many horses, and in a single day he is received three times.
judgment.meaning: The sun rises above the earth: light spreads, and everything becomes visible. The image is of a loyal noble, the Marquis of Kang, who serves his king so well that he is showered with gifts of horses and granted three audiences in one day. This is rapid, easy advancement that comes from trust between a capable person and a generous superior. It is favorable. You are noticed, valued and given room to grow. The key is that the prince is not seeking glory for himself; he brings peace to others and gives what he receives back into the common good. Keep your aims bright and unselfish, and the progress continues.

image.text: The sun rises over the earth: the image of Progress. The noble one makes their own bright nature shine.
image.meaning: The sun does not create its light from nothing; it simply comes out from behind the horizon. In the same way, your best qualities are already there, often obscured by doubt, habit or confusion. Progress here is the work of clearing them, so that your clarity and goodness can show. As you brighten what is true in yourself, your outer advancement follows naturally.

lines.text: Progressing, but held back. Staying steady brings good fortune. If you are not trusted, be generous and calm. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You start to move forward and meet resistance or simple disbelief; others are not yet sure of you. Do not push or protest. Keep doing what is right, calmly and with an open heart. Trust takes time to form, and it cannot be demanded. If you stay generous rather than resentful, you make no mistake, and the way will open when your reliability has become plain.

lines.text: Progressing, but in sorrow. Staying steady brings good fortune. Then you receive a great blessing from your grandmother.
lines.meaning: You are moving ahead, but you feel cut off from the one person who could open doors for you, and it makes you sad. Keep to your course with integrity. In time, help will come from a quiet, nurturing source, someone gentle and powerful who sees your worth, like a grandmother’s blessing. This line is yielding and central: patience and sincerity draw the support you need.

lines.text: Everyone is in agreement. Regret fades.
lines.meaning: You are not strong enough to advance alone, and that could be a source of regret. But you move together with others who share your aim, and their trust carries you. The group’s agreement makes up for what you lack. Working in harmony with the people around you, rather than going your own way, dissolves doubt and lets you progress. This is a good time for shared effort.

lines.text: Progressing like a big rat. Persisting is dangerous.
lines.meaning: This is a strong line in a position of influence, but it advances by grabbing and hoarding, like a rodent that sneaks forward and stores things for itself. Progress built on stealth, accumulation or unfair advantage cannot bear the light of the rising sun. If you keep going that way, it will become dangerous and you will be exposed. Look honestly at how you are moving ahead, and choose the open way.

lines.text: Regret fades. Do not take gain and loss to heart. Going forward brings good fortune. Everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: You hold the central, ruling place, and you lead with gentleness. Things could go either way in detail, but that is not what matters. Stop calculating every win and loss, and stop worrying about whether each step pays off. Act from your clarity and your goodwill, and let the results take care of themselves. Moving forward in that spirit brings good fortune all around.

lines.text: Progressing with the horns, using them only to discipline one’s own city. Awareness of danger brings good fortune; no mistake. But persisting brings shame.
lines.meaning: You are at the top, and advancing now means using force, like lowering your horns. That is acceptable only to set your own house in order: to correct your own faults or the people you are actually responsible for. Stay aware of the danger in harshness; then no mistake is made. But if you keep pressing with force, even in a good cause, it turns into humiliation. Use it briefly, then stop.

life.work: A good time for promotion, visibility and new responsibility; earn trust by bringing clarity and sharing credit.
life.love: Openness and warmth draw people toward you; be generous and transparent rather than calculating.
life.inner: Clear away what dims your own light; your progress begins with letting your better nature show.

question: What bright quality in me is ready to rise, and what is still hiding it?

name: Darkening of the Light
essence: The light has gone down into the earth: you are in a time when the unjust prevail and goodness is wounded. Keep your light hidden and burning within, and endure without giving up your principles.

judgment.text: Darkening of the Light. In hard times it is to your advantage to stay true.
judgment.meaning: Fire is below and Earth above: the sun has set and the land is dark. This is a time when a dark ruler holds power, when the honest are harmed and good intentions are punished. You cannot fight this openly without being destroyed. The ancient examples are King Wen, imprisoned by a tyrant, and Prince Ji, who feigned madness to survive while keeping his integrity. The counsel is to stay steadfast in difficulty: hold on to your principles inwardly, while outwardly you are careful, modest and even obscure. Hiding your light is not betrayal of it; it is how it survives. Nights end. What matters is that you are still yourself when the light returns.

image.text: The light has gone into the earth: the image of Darkening of the Light. The noble one lives among the people, keeps the light veiled, and in that very way remains clear.
image.meaning: When the sun is inside the earth, its light is still there, only covered. So too the wise person does not flaunt insight or point out everyone’s faults. They move among others quietly, tolerant and unassuming, without losing their own clarity. Sometimes being less visible is the only way to keep seeing truly. Discretion protects your light.

lines.text: Darkening of the light in flight: he lets his wings droop. The noble one on the road goes three days without eating. He has somewhere to go, but the host has words for him.
lines.meaning: You see the trouble early and choose to leave, with your wings lowered so as not to be noticed. The way out is costly: hardship, hunger, being misunderstood. People may gossip about why you left or say you are foolish. Do not be swayed. You saw what was coming, and you have a reason to go. Early withdrawal is painful now but spares you far worse later.

lines.text: Darkening of the light: he is wounded in the left thigh. He brings help with a strong horse. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are hurt, but not fatally; the left thigh is a wound that slows you, not one that stops you. Do not lose yourself in the pain. Instead, use what strength you have, quickly and wholeheartedly, to help others who are in danger too. This central, yielding line is loyal and balanced. Acting swiftly for the good of others, even while wounded, brings good fortune.

lines.text: Darkening of the light during the hunt in the south. The great leader of the darkness is captured. Do not expect to set everything right at once.
lines.meaning: This strong line, at the top of the bright inner trigram, faces the dark ruler at the top of the figure. By chance or by courage, you meet the source of the trouble directly and overcome it. But be careful: when a long darkness is broken, habits of disorder remain. Do not rush to correct everything overnight. Change that is forced too fast creates new damage. Restore order patiently.

lines.text: He enters the left side of the belly. He reaches the very heart of the darkening, and goes out through the gate and courtyard.
lines.meaning: You are close to the center of the darkness, near the one who causes it, and you come to understand its nature from the inside. Once you see clearly that it cannot be changed, you are free to leave, before the disaster arrives. Do not stay out of loyalty or hope. Knowing the heart of the problem is precisely what lets you walk out the gate.

lines.text: Darkening of the light as with Prince Ji. Staying true is to your advantage.
lines.meaning: Prince Ji lived at the court of the tyrant who was his own relative. He could not leave, so he hid his wisdom by pretending to be mad, and he kept his integrity safe within. You may be in a place you cannot escape. Then the way is to stay inwardly firm and outwardly inconspicuous. Hide your light, not your conscience. Unbending inner steadfastness is the advantage now.

lines.text: Not light but darkness. First he climbed to the heavens; then he plunged into the depths of the earth.
lines.meaning: This is the dark ruler himself, at the peak. He rose high, wounding the light in others, and in doing so he destroyed his own. Darkness that reaches its limit collapses by itself. If you are the one in power, see the warning: what you gain by harming others brings you down. If you suffer under such power, take heart: its fall comes when it has reached the top.

life.work: In a hostile or unjust workplace, keep your head down, protect your integrity, and do not provoke a fight you cannot win; plan your exit or your endurance carefully.
life.love: During painful times, be discreet and gentle; do not force truths that would only harm, and keep faith with your values.
life.inner: Keep your inner flame protected. You can be quiet on the outside and fully awake within.

question: In this dark time, how can I protect what I believe in without wearing it on my sleeve?

name: The Family
essence: Every person and every group needs a home ground where roles are clear and care is real. When the inner circle is in order, its influence spreads outward.

judgment.text: The Family. Steadfastness, as of the woman of the house, is favorable.
judgment.meaning: The figure shows a household in which each line is in its proper place: the yielding second line, the woman, at the center of the inner trigram; the strong fifth line, the man, at the center of the outer. The bonds of the family rest on loyalty, faithfulness and each person doing their part. The text singles out the steadfastness of the woman, who keeps the inner life of the home in order. Read broadly, it means that the stability of any close group, a family, team or circle of friends, depends on people who are faithful in the inner, unseen work. Order and warmth within lead to order without. Tend your own circle first.

image.text: Wind comes forth from Fire: the image of The Family. The noble one puts substance in their words and constancy in their conduct.
image.meaning: Fire within creates warmth and the wind that rises from it carries that warmth outward. Influence in a family works the same way: it starts within you and spreads. What you say has to be real and backed by what you do, and what you do has to be consistent over time. Children, partners and colleagues learn from what you live, not from what you announce.

lines.text: Firm boundaries within the family. Regret fades.
lines.meaning: At the very beginning of a household, a team or a new arrangement, set clear rules and expectations. If each person knows their place and the limits from the start, there is no later need for harsh correction, and no regret. Boundaries given early are a kindness. It is much harder to set them once bad habits have formed.

lines.text: She does not follow her whims. She sees to the food within. Steadfastness brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: Your role now is the quiet, central work of caring for others: feeding, sustaining and holding things together. It is not a time to go after personal impulses or outer ambitions. This line is yielding and central, attuned to the strong fifth line. Give yourself to the inner care that keeps everyone going. Its value is enormous even if it is little noticed. Steadiness here brings good fortune.

lines.text: When tempers run high in the family, being too severe brings regret, but still good fortune. When woman and child giggle and trifle, it ends in humiliation.
lines.meaning: There are two ways for a household to go wrong: too much strictness and too much laxity. Too much severity hurts, and you may regret it, yet on balance it is safer, because order holds. Too much indulgence, with everyone doing as they please, ends in disgrace. Seek the middle, but if you must err, err on the side of firm and fair discipline over chaos.

lines.text: She is the treasure of the house. Great good fortune.
lines.meaning: This yielding line sits next to the ruler and manages the resources of the household. It represents the one who keeps the home prosperous: careful with money, attentive to everyone’s needs, wise in dividing what there is. Good stewardship of shared resources and wellbeing brings great good fortune. If this is your role, embrace it; if someone else holds it, honor them.

lines.text: As a king he draws near to his family. Do not be anxious. Good fortune.
lines.meaning: This strong, central line is the head of the household, ruling not by fear but by the example of a generous, upright nature. A good leader of a family or team approaches the people in it with warmth and earns their love rather than their submission. Because the relationship is built on trust, there is nothing to worry about. Lead from character, and the household follows of its own accord.

lines.text: His work commands sincerity and respect. In the end, good fortune.
lines.meaning: At the top, the responsibility for the family’s order rests on the character of the one who leads it. If you are truthful and carry yourself with dignity, the people in your care trust you and take you seriously. This is not imposed; it comes from your being consistent over time. Such leadership has lasting results. In the end, things go well for everyone.

life.work: Clarify roles and responsibilities in your team; reliable everyday conduct builds a culture more than any memo.
life.love: Tend the home: shared meals, kept promises, warmth with fair boundaries; let your words match your actions.
life.inner: Bring order to your own inner household first; your habits are the foundation everything else rests on.

question: In my closest circle, where do my words and my everyday conduct not yet match?

name: Opposition
essence: People or forces are pulling in opposite directions. Large shared undertakings are not possible now, but small things can still go well, and differences can even become fruitful.

judgment.text: Opposition. In small matters, good fortune.
judgment.meaning: Fire rises upward and Lake water sinks downward; the two trigrams move apart. They are also two sisters living under one roof whose wishes do not meet. This is a time of estrangement, misunderstanding and difference: in a relationship, between colleagues, or within yourself. It is not a time for a grand joint project; trying to force unity will only drive things further apart. Yet the omen is not bad. Small, careful steps toward each other can still succeed. And opposition has its own use: heaven and earth are opposite, yet together they create; male and female differ, yet they unite. Respect the difference, work modestly, and seek connection where it is actually possible.

image.text: Above, Fire; below, the Lake: the image of Opposition. Amid all that they share with others, the noble one remains their own person.
image.meaning: Fire and water stay themselves even when placed together. In the same way, you can live and work among others, agree on common things and share in common life, without losing your own character. You do not need to merge with others or reject them. You can be in company and still be distinct. Hold to your own nature while remaining courteous and connected.

lines.text: Regret fades. If you lose your horse, do not run after it; it will come back by itself. When you meet a bad person, guard against mistakes.
lines.meaning: In a time of estrangement, chasing what has drifted away only drives it farther. Let it go. What truly belongs to you will return of its own accord, like a horse that comes back home. If you meet people with bad intentions, do not push them away harshly, which would make them enemies. Simply be courteous and careful. No mistake is made that way.

lines.text: He meets his lord in a narrow lane. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Misunderstanding has kept two people who belong together apart. Formal channels are blocked. But a chance meeting in an out-of-the-way place, an informal conversation or an unexpected opening, can bring you back together. Using such an indirect route is no mistake. This strong line in the center of the lower trigram corresponds with the ruler above; their connection is real, even if it has to be found through a side door.

lines.text: One sees the wagon dragged back, the oxen stopped, the man’s hair and nose cut off. Not a good beginning, but a good end.
lines.meaning: Everything seems to be against you: you are held back, blocked and even humiliated, like the driver punished and disfigured. It feels as if the whole world opposes you. But this yielding line is truly connected to the top line, and the bond survives. Hold on to the people and aims who are right for you. The beginning is bitter, but the outcome is good.

lines.text: Isolated by opposition, you meet a like-minded person, and you can trust each other. Danger, but no mistake.
lines.meaning: You are alone, at odds with those around you. Then you meet someone who shares your values, a kindred spirit or a person of real integrity. With them, you can be honest and build something in good faith. The situation remains risky, but this trust overcomes isolation. Join with the person who sees as you do, openly and sincerely. That is no mistake.

lines.text: Regret fades. The companion bites through the wrapping. If you go to him, how could it be a mistake?
lines.meaning: At first, you may not recognize the true friend; they are hidden, as though inside a skin. But the sincere person cuts through the outer layers of distrust and reaches you. When that happens, do not hold back. Go toward them. This yielding ruler is supported by the strong second line. Real help and real affection are available. Meeting them halfway leads to no regret.

lines.text: Isolated by opposition, you see your companion as a pig covered in mud, as a wagon full of devils. First you draw your bow, then you put it down. He is no robber; he comes to woo at the right time. As you go, rain falls, and good fortune follows.
lines.meaning: Isolation and suspicion have distorted your view. You see the very person who loves you as dirty or monstrous, and you prepare to fight. Then you recognize the truth: they are not an enemy but someone coming toward you in good faith. When the misunderstanding lifts, the tension breaks like rain after a heavy sky. Put down the bow, and good fortune follows.

life.work: Do not force a big joint initiative with people who disagree; agree on small, concrete steps and respect different styles.
life.love: Look for a small, sincere gesture rather than demanding full agreement; check whether your suspicion distorts what you see.
life.inner: You can belong and still be yourself; notice where you treat difference as a threat.

question: Where am I seeing an enemy where there may be a friend, and what small step could close the distance?

name: Obstruction
essence: The way ahead is blocked: danger before you, a steep mountain behind. Pushing forward is not the answer. Stop, turn inward, gather allies, and find the open way around.

judgment.text: Obstruction. The southwest is favorable; the northeast is not. It is good to see the great person. Staying true brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: Water lies ahead of you and a mountain stands at your back: you cannot easily go forward or back. The text points to the southwest, which is the region of open plains and of the receptive Earth, and away from the northeast, the region of mountains. In other words, take the easy, yielding road, not the steep one; work with others, rather than striving alone against the barrier. See the great person: seek out someone with wisdom and authority to guide you. And remain steadfast in your aims. Obstacles are not punishment; they are a summons to stop, look honestly at yourself, and find a better path. Handled this way, they lead to good fortune.

image.text: Water on the mountain: the image of Obstruction. The noble one turns inward and cultivates character.
image.meaning: Water on a mountain cannot run freely; it collects and is slowed by the rock. When outer progress is blocked, the wise person does not blame circumstances or beat against them. Instead they look within: what in me contributes to this? What needs to grow? Obstruction becomes an occasion for self-examination and self-improvement. When you change, the obstacle often changes with you.

lines.text: Going leads into obstruction; coming back brings praise.
lines.meaning: You are at the beginning, and the way ahead is blocked. If you push forward now, you walk straight into trouble. If you hold back and wait for the right moment, you will be recognized for your good judgment. This is not failure but wisdom. Pause, observe and prepare. Know when not to go.

lines.text: The king’s servant meets obstruction upon obstruction. It is not his own doing.
lines.meaning: Here you cannot avoid the difficulty, because duty puts you in its path. You serve someone or something greater, and you must face obstacle after obstacle on their behalf. This is not your fault, and you are not to blame. The line is yielding and central, loyally connected to the ruler. Keep going in good conscience. Sometimes struggle is the price of faithfulness.

lines.text: Going leads into obstruction, so he comes back.
lines.meaning: This strong line at the top of the inner trigram could charge forward, but there is danger ahead. Turn back instead, to those who depend on you, the two yielding lines below. Returning home is not weakness; it is where your strength is needed and appreciated. Look after your own people, and let them support you. That is the better use of your energy now.

lines.text: Going leads into obstruction; coming back brings union.
lines.meaning: You cannot overcome this alone. Advancing now leads straight into difficulty. Pull back and connect with others who can help: gather allies, build trust, and create the circle of support you need. Shared effort will do what solitary striving cannot. When the right people are joined together, the obstacle can be faced.

lines.text: In the midst of the greatest obstruction, friends come.
lines.meaning: You are at the center of the danger, in the position of leadership, and the difficulty is at its worst. You cannot retreat because others depend on you. Yet because you hold firm and your cause is right, help arrives: people come to your side. Your steadfastness draws them. Stay centered and lead. You do not face this alone.

lines.text: Going leads into obstruction; coming back brings great good fortune. It is good to see the great person.
lines.meaning: You have come through, and you might be tempted to walk away from the struggle that others still face. Do not. Turn back and use what you have learned to help those still caught in it. Seek out a wise leader and work together with them. Returning to the common task, rather than going off alone, brings great good fortune.

life.work: If a project is stalled, stop pushing; consult a mentor, gather allies and look for an easier route rather than the hardest one.
life.love: When things are stuck between you, ask what you contribute to the impasse before you ask the other to change.
life.inner: Treat the obstacle as a mirror: what in your attitude or habits is it showing you?

question: What is this obstacle asking me to change in myself, and who could help me through?

name: Deliverance
essence: The storm breaks and the tension is released. Now the work is to clear away what remains of the trouble quickly, forgive, and return to an ordinary, easy life.

judgment.text: Deliverance. The southwest is favorable. If nothing more needs to be done, returning brings good fortune. If something still needs to be done, acting quickly brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: Thunder above, rain below: the long-gathering storm finally breaks, and the air clears. Obstacles dissolve and tension is released. The southwest, as before, means the open, easy plain: after deliverance, do not stay tense or push; go back to calm, simple ways. The text gives two counsels. If the problem is truly solved, return to normal life and do not stir things up again. If there is still something to finish, do it quickly, without delay, so that nothing festers. Deliverance is a moment of relief that should be used wisely. Clear up quickly, then rest.

image.text: Thunder and rain set in: the image of Deliverance. The noble one pardons mistakes and forgives wrongs.
image.meaning: After a thunderstorm, the air is clean and everything starts fresh. In the same way, once a hard time has passed, the wise person does not hold grudges or punish old faults. They let go of mistakes and forgive wrongs, so that people can begin again. Forgiveness is how you finish the release. Clinging to resentment keeps the storm hanging overhead.

lines.text: No mistake.
lines.meaning: The tension is breaking. You are at the beginning of the release, with support from a strong line above you. Nothing needs to be said or done beyond keeping quiet and letting the relief settle. Rest, recover, and do not create new complications. The simplest course is correct now, and there is no mistake in it.

lines.text: In the field he kills three foxes and receives a yellow arrow. Staying steady brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: Foxes are the cunning ones who whisper, flatter and mislead. Here you clear them out of the field: you deal firmly with deceit and bad influences around you. The yellow arrow stands for the straight, central way, balanced and honest. Remove what corrupts, but do it by being upright, not by cunning of your own. Steadfastness brings good fortune.

lines.text: He carries a load on his back and yet rides in a carriage, and so he invites robbers. Persisting brings humiliation.
lines.meaning: You have come out of difficulty into an easier, more comfortable position, but you behave as though you were above your station: a porter riding in a gentleman’s carriage. Showing off, or holding a place you have not yet grown into, attracts envy and trouble. If you keep this up, it ends in shame. Be modest, match your conduct to your real place, and the danger passes.

lines.text: Free yourself from your big toe. Then a companion comes, and you can trust him.
lines.meaning: The big toe is the first line, a weak, clinging element attached to you at the lowest level: hangers-on, bad habits, people who use you. As long as you keep them close, people of real worth stay away. Let go of these dependencies. When you do, true companions arrive, people you can rely on, and real trust becomes possible.

lines.text: If only the noble one can free himself, good fortune. This proves to petty people that he is in earnest.
lines.meaning: You are in the ruling position, and the trouble now lies within your own circle: inferior influences, or your own lesser tendencies. Only you can release yourself from them, by an inner decision. When you do, others see that you mean it, and those who would drag you down give up and withdraw on their own. Your firm resolve is what frees you and everyone around you.

lines.text: The prince shoots at a hawk on a high wall and brings it down. Everything is favorable.
lines.meaning: The hawk sits on a high wall: a powerful, entrenched obstacle, the last one standing in the way of full deliverance. The prince does not hurry; he prepares his bow and shoots when the moment is right. With good aim and timing, you can remove even an obstacle that seems out of reach. Get ready inwardly, wait for the moment, then act decisively. Everything goes well.

life.work: Tie up loose ends quickly after a crisis, then return to normal rhythm; do not go hunting for the next battle.
life.love: Forgive what happened during the hard time, and let both of you start fresh.
life.inner: Release the tension your body and mind still hold; let go of grudges, old guilt and clinging habits.

question: Now that the pressure is lifting, what do I need to forgive or release so I can truly begin again?

name: Decrease
essence: Something has to be reduced: spending, ambition, ego, excess. Done honestly and for the right reason, giving up is not loss but a deeper kind of wealth.

judgment.text: Decrease, carried out with sincerity, brings the highest good fortune and no mistake. You can stay steady in it, and it is good to have a goal. How should it be done? Two simple bowls are enough for the offering.
judgment.meaning: This is a time of less: less money, less energy, fewer options, or a deliberate choice to cut back. The hexagram shows the lower trigram, the Lake, giving something of itself to build up the Mountain above. What is taken from below enriches what is above. Such a shift can feel like hardship, but the text promises great good fortune, on one condition: sincerity. If the reduction is honest and serves something real, it does not harm you. The image of the two bowls says it plainly. When resources are thin, a small offering made with a true heart counts for as much as a lavish one. Do not pretend to more than you have. Strip things back to what matters, give what you can without show, and keep moving toward your aim. Simplicity is not a failure here; it is the right form for the moment.

image.text: Below the mountain lies the lake: the image of Decrease. The noble one holds back anger and reins in desire.
image.meaning: The lake at the foot of the mountain evaporates and feeds the slopes above; the mountain, in turn, is rooted by the lake. Something lower is given up so that something higher can stand. In a person, the things best reduced are the hot, restless ones: anger that flares like a mountain storm and desire that keeps wanting more. The practice is to notice them early and let them cool, so that your strength goes into what you actually value.

lines.text: When your own work is done, go quickly to help. No mistake. But weigh carefully how much you can give.
lines.meaning: Someone above you, or someone close, needs your help, and you are in a position to give it. Finish what is yours, then go without delay; holding back would be wrong. But be careful. Generosity that empties you completely helps no one for long. Before you commit, measure how much you can spare of your time, money or energy, and give that much freely and promptly.

lines.text: Staying firm is favorable. Setting out to act would go badly. You can increase others without decreasing yourself.
lines.meaning: You are asked, perhaps pressed, to sacrifice something of your own integrity to please or serve another. Do not. Your best contribution is to stay steady and true to your position; rushing off to give yourself away would bring misfortune. Paradoxically, by not diminishing yourself you benefit the other person more. A firm, reliable presence is a gift in itself. Keep your center.

lines.text: When three people travel together, one will be lost. When one person travels alone, they find a companion.
lines.meaning: This is a line about the natural arithmetic of closeness. Three is a crowd: in a trio someone ends up on the outside, and the group shrinks to a pair. One on their own, by contrast, finds a partner. Real bonds tend to form between two who are wholly committed to each other. If a relationship or alliance is losing a member, it may be finding its true shape. If you are alone, a companion is coming.

lines.text: Reduce your illness. If you send for help quickly, there will be joy. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Something unhealthy is holding you back: a bad habit, a fault, a grudge, a real physical problem you have been ignoring. The decrease that is called for is to shrink that ailment. Act fast and accept help; friends and advisers are ready to support you once you admit what is wrong. Dealt with promptly, the trouble lifts and gladness follows. Delay only lets it settle in.

lines.text: Someone enriches you with ten pairs of tortoise shells, and you cannot refuse. Supreme good fortune.
lines.meaning: Tortoise shells were precious, used for divination and worth a fortune. This is the ruler’s line, yielding and open, and because it asks for nothing and is humble at the center, blessings arrive that cannot be turned away. Help, recognition or good luck comes to you without your forcing it. Accept it gracefully. What you gave up earlier has made room for this. It is a mark of being in harmony with the time.

lines.text: Increase without decreasing anyone. No mistake. Steadiness brings good fortune; it is good to have a goal. You gain helpers who are not bound to any one household.
lines.meaning: Decrease has run its course and turned into its opposite. You are now in a position to benefit others without taking anything from anyone. Generosity of this kind wins people who serve the common good rather than private ties. Use your position to give widely and steadily. Keep your aim clear and keep going. People will gather around your work because it serves everyone.

life.work: Trim the budget, the schedule or the scope down to what truly matters, and present what you have honestly rather than dressing it up.
life.love: Give what you genuinely can, without overextending, and let go of resentments and demands that weigh on the bond.
life.inner: Cool your anger and quiet your wanting; less inner noise leaves more room for what you care about.

question: What could you let go of, honestly and without show, that would make room for something truer?

name: Increase
essence: A time of gain, when what flows down from above enriches those below. Use the momentum to act boldly, help others, and become better yourself.

judgment.text: Increase. It is favorable to have somewhere to go. It is favorable to cross the great river.
judgment.meaning: This is the mirror of Decrease. Here something is taken from above and given to below: the strong line that once sat at the top has moved down to the base, strengthening the foundation. When those in a higher position share their resources with those beneath them, everyone gains, and the whole structure grows. For you this is a season of momentum. Opportunities open, support arrives and energy is available. The text says it is favorable to set out and even to cross the great river, the old image for a major, risky undertaking. Such times do not last forever, so use this one. Begin the large project, make the difficult move, extend your help to others. Increase is best spent, not hoarded: what you give onward keeps the current flowing.

image.text: Wind and thunder: the image of Increase. When the noble one sees what is good, they move toward it; when they see a fault in themselves, they correct it.
image.meaning: Thunder and wind strengthen each other: the storm’s shock drives the wind on, and the wind carries the thunder further. Inner growth works the same way. When you see a good example, follow it at once, with the speed of wind. When you find something wrong in yourself, change it, with the decisiveness of thunder. Each act of improvement makes the next one easier. That is the most reliable increase there is.

lines.text: It is favorable to use this to undertake great work. Supreme good fortune and no mistake.
lines.meaning: You are at the beginning, and strength has come to you from above: backing, resources, a mandate. Use it for something substantial, not something small. Because you are starting from a low position, the large undertaking must be done well and for the right reasons; only then is it beyond reproach. If you succeed, the good fortune is great and no one can fault you. Aim high and work selflessly.

lines.text: Someone enriches you with ten pairs of tortoise shells, and you cannot refuse. Lasting steadiness brings good fortune. The king makes an offering to the Lord on High: good fortune.
lines.meaning: Blessings come unasked because you are receptive and centered. Accept them, but stay constant; the good fortune depends on not letting success change you. The image of the king’s offering to heaven says that gain should be received with gratitude and linked to something higher than yourself. Remember where it came from, use it in a spirit of service, and the increase will last.

lines.text: You are enriched through unfortunate events. No mistake. If you are sincere and walk the middle path, report to the prince with your jade tablet of office.
lines.meaning: Benefit is reaching you by way of trouble: a setback, a crisis, a hard assignment. Difficulty, handled well, gives you experience, standing and authority you would not have earned otherwise. No one can blame you for gaining this way. But be transparent. Act in good faith, keep to the reasonable middle, and keep the people above you properly informed, as an official would bring a jade tablet to vouch for his word.

lines.text: If you walk the middle path and report to the prince, he will follow your advice. It is favorable to be relied upon in moving the capital.
lines.meaning: You stand between those above and those below, and both trust you because you are fair. Speak honestly to the person in charge, and your counsel will be heard. You may be entrusted with something as large as relocating a capital: a restructuring, a move, a major change that affects many. Such a task needs someone without a private agenda. Be that person, and the shift will benefit everyone.

lines.text: If you have a truly kind heart, do not ask. Supreme good fortune. Sincere people will recognize your kindness as your virtue.
lines.meaning: This is the ruler of Increase, and the deepest benefit comes from real goodwill, not from calculation. Do not ask whether your kindness will be repaid or whether it is working; simply be kind and generous. Such sincerity is unmistakable, and people respond to it with loyalty and trust. You do not need to advertise your good intentions. They are felt. The fortune here is the highest.

lines.text: No one increases him; someone may even strike him. He sets his heart but does not keep it steady. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: At the top, increase has turned to greed. Whoever only takes, and forgets to give, is soon isolated: no one helps them, and someone may attack. The line warns against a heart that keeps changing its commitments and serves only itself. If you are reaching for more without sharing, stop. Steady your intentions and turn your attention back to what you can offer. Otherwise this goes badly.

life.work: Momentum is on your side: start the ambitious project and share credit and resources with those who help you.
life.love: Be generous without counting the cost, and let your care for each other make both of you better.
life.inner: Follow the good you see in others and fix your own faults as soon as you notice them.

question: How can you use what is coming to you to help someone else grow as well?

name: Breakthrough
essence: One last negative element remains, and the time has come to remove it. Do it openly and resolutely, but without violence or arrogance.

judgment.text: Breakthrough. Make the matter known at the king’s court. Declare it truthfully, though there is danger. Inform your own city; it is not favorable to take up arms. It is favorable to have somewhere to go.
judgment.meaning: Five strong lines are rising beneath a single weak one at the top. The bad element is almost gone, and a decisive push will finish it. The hexagram is about how to make that push. First, bring the matter into the open: name the problem in the proper place, honestly, even though that carries risk. Second, begin with your own side, setting your own house in order and winning those around you. Third, do not resort to force. Fighting the wrong with its own weapons drags you down to its level and gives it new life. The breakthrough comes through clarity, steady pressure and a good example. Then you can move forward. Stay alert: even a weak opponent can strike back if you become careless or self-righteous.

image.text: The lake has risen up to heaven: the image of Breakthrough. The noble one shares wealth with those below and is wary of resting on their own virtue.
image.meaning: A lake lifted into the sky must break and pour down as rain. What has built up at the top has to be released. The wise person, seeing this, does not hoard: they let their resources and good fortune flow down to others before the pressure bursts. They also refuse to sit on their merit. Pride accumulates like water behind a dam, and the self-satisfied are the next to be swept away.

lines.text: Strength in the toes, pressing forward. If you go and are not equal to the task, you make a mistake.
lines.meaning: You are eager to push ahead at the very start, but your power is all in your toes: forward lean without footing. Charging into the fight before you have the means to win it will bring a setback, and it will be your own fault. Measure your strength honestly against what you face. Resolve is good; premature action is not. Wait until you can carry it through.

lines.text: Cries of alarm. Armed men in the evening and in the night. Do not be afraid.
lines.meaning: You are resolute but careful, and that combination makes you safe. Danger may come suddenly, at night, when you least expect it. Because you have stayed alert and prepared, sounding the alarm and keeping your guard up, you need not fear it. Keep your vigilance quiet and constant. Inner watchfulness, not anxiety, is what lets you meet a surprise without being thrown.

lines.text: Strength showing in the cheekbones: misfortune. The noble one is firmly resolved. Walking alone, they are caught in the rain and soaked, and people resent them. No mistake.
lines.meaning: If your determination shows on your face as hostility, it goes badly; you tip off the opponent and alarm others. This line has ties to the weak line at the top and may appear to be on the wrong side. Hold your resolve inwardly. You may have to stay in contact with the problem, get wet in its rain and endure the suspicion of allies who misread you. As long as your inner purpose is clear, you are not at fault.

lines.text: There is no skin on his thighs, and he walks with difficulty. If he let himself be led like a sheep, his regret would vanish. But he hears these words and does not believe them.
lines.meaning: You are restless and cannot settle, yet pushing ahead keeps hurting you. The advice is to stop insisting on going first and to follow along, the way a sheep is easy to lead from behind. If you did, the trouble would disappear. The line predicts, though, that you will hear this and not accept it. Stubbornness is the real obstacle. Be the exception: listen.

lines.text: Weeds in the garden: uproot them with full resolve. Walking the middle path, no mistake.
lines.meaning: The image is a tenacious plant, purslane, that grows back from the smallest root. You are closest to the problem and may even feel some attachment to it, which makes decisive action hard. Yet it must be cleared out completely, not trimmed. Do it firmly but without extremes, keeping to the balanced middle. Only then are you free of blame. Half measures invite the weed back.

lines.text: No call for help. In the end, misfortune.
lines.meaning: The last weak element has nowhere left to hide, and no one comes when it calls. For you this can mean two things. If you are the one clinging to something outworn, recognize that its time is over; resisting only prolongs the fall. If you are dealing with such an element, do not relax at the moment of seeming victory. A remnant left behind can grow again. Finish the work thoroughly.

life.work: Raise the problem openly with the right people, set your own team straight first, and win by argument and example rather than by fighting.
life.love: Speak the difficult truth calmly and kindly; do not let it come out as an attack.
life.inner: Uproot the stubborn habit completely, and beware of becoming proud of your own righteousness.

question: What needs to be named openly now, and how can you do it firmly without hostility?

name: Coming to Meet
essence: An unexpected meeting with a force that seems small but can quickly take over. Recognize it early, keep it in its place, and do not give yourself to it.

judgment.text: Coming to Meet. The woman is powerful. Do not marry such a woman.
judgment.meaning: A single yielding line has suddenly appeared at the base, beneath five strong ones. It looks weak and harmless, but it is the start of a reversal: from here, the dark will grow line by line. The old text pictures it as a bold woman who meets many men and dominates them. The point is not about women; it is about any influence that seems minor and attractive, slips in easily, and then takes control. That may be a person, a habit, a compromise or a deal that sounds too good. Encounters of this kind cannot always be avoided, and the meeting itself is not wrong. What would be wrong is to bind yourself to it, to marry it. Stay friendly, stay clear, and do not give it a permanent place in your life.

image.text: Under heaven, there is wind: the image of Coming to Meet. The ruler issues commands and announces them to the four quarters.
image.meaning: Wind blows everywhere beneath the sky, touching all things and carrying influence far. A ruler uses this to spread clear instructions through the whole land. Influence will reach people in any case; the question is whose. If you hold responsibility, make your intentions known plainly and widely, so that the people who depend on you are not left open to whatever passing current comes along.

lines.text: It must be tied to a brake of bronze. Steadiness brings good fortune. If you let it go forward, you will see misfortune. A lean pig is restless and keeps pacing.
lines.meaning: The dark element has only just entered, and this is the moment to stop it. Clamp on the brake now, firmly, as you would brake a cart before it rolls downhill. If you let it run, trouble follows. Do not be misled by how thin and weak it looks: the half-starved pig is exactly the one that keeps straining to break out. Small temptations are the most restless. Hold them back early.

lines.text: There is a fish in the bundle. No mistake. It is not favorable for guests.
lines.meaning: You have the problem in hand, wrapped up like a fish in a packet, and you are keeping it under gentle control. That is no fault. But do not pass it on or let it come into contact with others; it would cause them harm. Contain the difficult influence yourself, quietly, rather than letting it spread to guests, colleagues or the wider circle.

lines.text: There is no skin on his thighs, and he walks with difficulty. Danger, but no great mistake.
lines.meaning: You are drawn toward an involvement, but circumstances keep blocking you, and you cannot settle. It is uncomfortable and you hesitate. That is actually a protection. Because you cannot get close to the questionable influence, you are spared a real error. Be aware of the danger in your own wish to rush in, and accept the delay as a blessing.

lines.text: There is no fish in the bundle. If you rise up now, misfortune.
lines.meaning: You have kept a distance from those beneath you, and now when you need their support it is not there. The fish is gone from the packet. If you try to start something or assert yourself now, it will go badly. The lesson is about connection. Do not be too proud to stay in touch with ordinary people and modest helpers; without them you have nothing to hold.

lines.text: A melon wrapped in willow leaves. Hidden brilliance. It falls as if from heaven.
lines.meaning: Ripe fruit spoils easily; the shady leaves protect it. You are in a strong position facing what is weaker or more fragile than you. Shelter it rather than dominate it, and keep your own excellence modest and concealed. Do not force things. When the time is ripe, what you hope for will drop into your hands as if sent from above. Patience and inner quality bring it.

lines.text: Meeting with the horns. Humiliation, but no mistake.
lines.meaning: At the top, aloof and proud, you meet others horns first: rejecting, butting away whatever approaches. This is awkward and may make people think you cold, and it costs you something. Yet withdrawing from a bad influence is not wrong in itself. Keep your boundaries, but recognize that your coolness has a price, and soften your manner where you can.

life.work: Be wary of the offer, partner or shortcut that looks minor but could take over; deal with it early and set clear terms.
life.love: A strong attraction is not the same as a lasting bond; enjoy the meeting but do not commit yourself to what overwhelms you.
life.inner: Catch the first small slip of a bad habit and brake it before it gathers speed.

question: What small influence has just entered your life, and how much power are you willing to give it?

name: Gathering Together
essence: People are coming together around a common center. For a gathering to hold, it needs a worthy leader, sincere hearts, shared ritual and readiness for the unexpected.

judgment.text: Gathering Together. Success. The king goes to his ancestral temple. It is favorable to see the great person. Success; steadiness is favorable. Making a great offering brings good fortune. It is favorable to have somewhere to go.
judgment.meaning: The lake gathers on the earth: water collects where the land is low and welcoming. So people collect around a center that unites them. The hexagram lists what makes a gathering succeed. The king going to his temple is the connection to roots and shared values, the thing that makes a group more than a crowd. Seeing the great person means having a leader of real character at the core. Steadiness is needed, because groups come together on principle and fall apart on convenience. A great offering, generous and wholehearted, honors the moment and shows commitment. When these are present, the gathering is fortunate and can undertake something together. If you are forming a team, a family occasion or a movement, give it a true center, not just a reason to meet.

image.text: The lake rises above the earth: the image of Gathering Together. The noble one renews their weapons to be ready for the unforeseen.
image.meaning: When water gathers higher than the land, a flood becomes possible. Wherever many people or many resources come together, so does the risk of conflict, theft or sudden trouble. The wise person does not wait for that to happen. They keep their tools in good repair and their plans prepared. Being ready for the unexpected is not distrust of the group; it is what keeps it safe.

lines.text: You are sincere, but not to the end, so now there is confusion, now gathering. If you call out, a single handclasp turns things to laughter. Do not worry. Going on is no mistake.
lines.meaning: You want to join the right people, but you waver. You are swayed by those around you, and your commitment comes and goes. Do not stay stuck in that confusion. Reach out openly to the one you truly belong with. A simple, honest gesture, a call or a handshake, can turn awkwardness into shared laughter. Do not fear looking foolish. Moving toward the connection is right.

lines.text: Being drawn in brings good fortune and no mistake. If you are sincere, even a small offering is favorable.
lines.meaning: You are being drawn toward a group or a person by a deeper affinity, almost without effort. Let yourself be led there; it is fortunate. Do not feel you need grand gestures to belong. In the old rites, a modest seasonal offering was enough when the heart was true. Inner sincerity matters more than outward show. Simply show up as you are.

lines.text: Gathering with sighs. Nothing is favorable. Going on is no mistake, though there is slight regret.
lines.meaning: You want to belong, but you find yourself on the outside, and you sigh over it. Nothing in your present circle seems to work. Do not give up and do not keep pining. Move toward someone closer to the center who can bring you in, even if it means swallowing a little pride. There may be some embarrassment, but going is still right.

lines.text: Great good fortune. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You are gathering people together on behalf of someone above you, or for a shared cause, and you are not seeking it for yourself. This kind of gathering, offered in service, is fortunate. The text is brief because the condition is simple: your position is strong but not central, so your success is blameless only if it truly serves the larger whole. Keep your motives clean and the good fortune is great.

lines.text: Gathering around a position of authority. No mistake. If some do not yet trust it, sustained, lasting steadiness makes regret vanish.
lines.meaning: People gather around you because of your role, but not all of them believe in you yet. Your title alone will not win their trust. Keep to what is right, be consistent, and let your character show over time. As your integrity becomes obvious, doubt gives way and the gathering becomes real. Steadiness over the long haul is what dissolves regret.

lines.text: Sighing and lamenting, with tears and running nose. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You want to unite with others but find yourself alone and misunderstood, and the sorrow of it overwhelms you. The text does not scold you for grieving; grief at being cut off is honest. Express it. Because your longing for connection is sincere, you are not at fault, and your sorrow may move others to reach out. Let your feelings bring you back toward people.

life.work: Give the team a clear shared purpose and a trusted leader, and plan ahead for problems before they arrive.
life.love: Shared rituals and simple gestures of sincerity hold people together better than grand declarations.
life.inner: Gather your scattered energies around what you most value, and keep yourself prepared for surprises.

question: What is the true center that holds your people together, and how can you strengthen it?

name: Pushing Upward
essence: Like a tree rising from the earth, you grow upward through steady, patient effort. Success is achievable; keep going and seek the right help.

judgment.text: Pushing Upward brings supreme success. Seek out the great person. Do not worry. Setting out toward the south brings good fortune.
judgment.meaning: The lower trigram is Wind, which also means wood; above it is Earth. The image is a sapling pushing up through soil. It does not force its way or leap; it bends around obstacles and grows a little each day, until it stands tall. That is the shape of your advance. The way upward is open, and great success is promised, but it comes through modest, continuous effort, not through a single dramatic move. Look for people with influence and wisdom who can help you, and approach them without anxiety; you have the merit to be received. The south, in the old tradition, stood for light, warmth and work. Head toward activity and achievement. Do not fret about the pace. Growth that is steady and adaptable is the kind that cannot be stopped.

image.text: Within the earth, wood grows: the image of Pushing Upward. The noble one, with yielding virtue, piles up small things until they become high and great.
image.meaning: A tree grows imperceptibly, ring by ring, adapting to stones and seasons, and one day it is tall. Character and achievement grow the same way. The wise person does not wait for a great leap. They add small good acts, small skills and small kept promises, day after day, flexibly and without pride. The accumulation is what becomes greatness.

lines.text: Pushing upward, welcomed and trusted. Great good fortune.
lines.meaning: You are at the bottom, but you are in tune with those above you, and they make room for you to rise. Your humble beginning is not a handicap; it is the root. Work hard, accept the trust being offered, and let others draw you upward. The good fortune is great because your rise is natural and supported, not forced.

lines.text: If you are sincere, even a small offering is favorable. No mistake.
lines.meaning: You are strong and capable, but you are not in a showy position, and you may lack polish or the usual credentials. That does not matter. As with a modest seasonal rite, genuine sincerity is enough. Present yourself honestly, without trying to impress, and you will be accepted by those you need. The connection rests on character, not on display.

lines.text: Pushing upward into an empty city.
lines.meaning: Nothing stands in your way. You move up as easily as entering a deserted town. Go ahead: the opportunity is real. But the image carries a quiet question. Why is the city empty? Things that come too easily can be hollow, or can leave you unprepared for later difficulty. Advance, but stay thoughtful and do not take the ease for granted.

lines.text: The king makes an offering on Mount Qi. Good fortune, no mistake.
lines.meaning: Mount Qi was the sacred mountain of the Zhou ancestors. You have been raised to a place of honor, close to the source of power, and invited to share in something meaningful. Accept it with reverence and devotion. Serve the larger purpose rather than your own advancement, and help others rise as well. Then your position is fortunate and no one can fault it.

lines.text: Steadiness brings good fortune. You climb the steps.
lines.meaning: You have reached a high place, and progress continues, step by step, like climbing the stairs of a great hall. The climb is orderly and your rise is secure. The warning is against haste or getting carried away. Stay calm and consistent, take each step properly, and do not skip any. Your steadiness is what makes this good fortune lasting.

lines.text: Pushing upward in darkness. It is favorable to be ceaselessly steady.
lines.meaning: You keep pushing upward, but you have lost sight of where you are going. Ambition that never stops becomes blind and exhausting. Recognize that you are near the top of what this effort can achieve. Turn your persistence into something sound: steady commitment to what is right rather than a drive for more. Unrelenting integrity is the only climbing that still helps you here.

life.work: Advance steadily rather than dramatically, seek out mentors and decision-makers, and let consistent effort build your standing.
life.love: Grow the relationship through small daily attentions; it deepens most when nothing is forced.
life.inner: Trust the slow accumulation of good habits, and bend around obstacles instead of fighting them.

question: What small step can you take today that adds to the larger growth you want?

name: Exhaustion
essence: You are trapped, drained or not believed. Outward means fail, but inner steadiness can turn the trial into success.

judgment.text: Exhaustion. Success. Steadiness. For the great person, good fortune and no mistake. When you speak, you are not believed.
judgment.meaning: The lake is above and the water has drained out below it: a lake with no water, a body without strength. The strong lines are hemmed in by weak ones. This is a time of pressure, depletion or oppression, when your efforts seem to go nowhere and your resources run dry. Yet the Judgment says success. Adversity does not ruin a person of real character; it tests and deepens them. If you stay steady and keep your spirit, you will come through, and you will be stronger for it. The great person does well here precisely because they do not collapse. One warning is specific: you will not be believed. Explanations, complaints and arguments will fall on deaf ears now. Save your words. Let your conduct speak, and hold on inwardly.

image.text: A lake with no water: the image of Exhaustion. The noble one stakes their life on carrying out their purpose.
image.meaning: When the lake has drained away, there is nothing left to draw on from outside. What remains is the person and their resolve. The wise person accepts this and decides to stay true to their purpose even at the highest cost. External circumstances can strip much away, but not your will to do what is right. That commitment is the water that does not run out.

lines.text: Your buttocks are pinned against a bare tree stump. You wander into a dark valley and for three years see no one.
lines.meaning: You are sitting on a hard place with no comfort and no shelter, and you are sinking into gloom. The danger of this line is that you let adversity pull you down into despair and isolation, cutting yourself off for a long time. Do not withdraw into the darkness. Recognize the mood for what it is, and take a step toward light and people before it hardens into years.

lines.text: Exhausted in the midst of wine and food. The man with red knee-bands is just coming. It is favorable to make offerings. Setting out would go badly. No mistake.
lines.meaning: Your trouble is not outward hardship; you have comfort enough. It is a weariness of spirit, a lack of meaning. Help is on its way: someone in authority, marked by the red knee-bands of office, will come to call on your abilities. Until then, prepare inwardly, as one prepares for a rite. Do not force your way out by acting rashly; that would go badly. Waiting is no mistake.

lines.text: Hemmed in by rock, leaning on thorns and thistles. You enter your house and do not find your wife. Misfortune.
lines.meaning: You push against what cannot be moved and lean on what wounds you. Restless and unwise, you make your own trap worse, and when you come home for comfort, it is gone. The line describes the misfortune of handling hardship badly: fighting the wrong obstacles and relying on the wrong supports. Stop pushing and stop leaning. Look honestly at what is actually holding you.

lines.text: He comes very slowly, hemmed in by a golden carriage. Humiliation, but it comes to an end.
lines.meaning: You want to help someone in need, but you are slowed down by wealth, rank or the people around you, the gilded carriage of your own position. Your delay is embarrassing and may be misread. Still, your intention is good and the connection is real. Keep going, even slowly. In the end you will arrive, and the awkwardness will pass.

lines.text: His nose and feet are cut off. He is oppressed by the man with crimson knee-bands. Joy comes slowly. It is favorable to make offerings.
lines.meaning: You hold a position of responsibility and wish to help, but you are hampered from above and below, as if maimed; even your own officials obstruct you. Do not despair. Little by little, things will improve. In the meantime, steady yourself inwardly. The image of offering points to devotion and composure: keep faith with your purpose and do what is right, and the turn will come.

lines.text: Tangled in creeping vines, on a shaky ledge. You tell yourself, “If I move, I will regret it,” and so you regret it. Going forward brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: The trap is nearly gone. What still holds you are thin vines and your own nervousness. You hesitate because you fear making things worse, and that very fear keeps you stuck. Admit that your past mistakes have made you overcautious, and resolve to move. Once you act decisively, you break free. Going forward now is fortunate.

life.work: When you are blocked and unheard, stop arguing your case and keep doing solid work; the situation will turn.
life.love: In a draining time, actions of loyalty say more than explanations, which may not be heard right now.
life.inner: Hold to your purpose when outward support runs dry; it is what carries you through.

question: When everything outside is depleted, what in you still holds?

name: The Well
essence: The well is the unchanging source that nourishes everyone. Keep it clean, reach all the way down, and do not let your vessel break.

judgment.text: The Well. The town can be moved, but not the well. It neither loses nor gains. People come and go and draw from it. If the rope does not quite reach the water, or the jug breaks, misfortune.
judgment.meaning: Wood below water: a wooden bucket lowered into a spring, bringing water up. Towns are rebuilt and moved, governments change, fashions come and go, but the well stays where it is and supplies the same water to everyone who comes. It is the image of what is lasting in human life: the deep sources of nourishment, wisdom and character that every generation draws on. Its water is never exhausted and never overflows. The danger is not in the well but in the drawing. If the rope is too short and you stop just above the water, or your jug cracks, you get nothing. For you, this means going deep enough. Do not settle for a shallow understanding or half an effort. Look after your tools, your training and your character, so that what you draw can actually reach people.

image.text: Above the wood is water: the image of The Well. The noble one encourages people in their work and urges them to help one another.
image.meaning: Plants draw water upward through their wood, from root to leaf, and a well bucket does the same. Water is shared and lifted through cooperation. The wise person organizes a community the same way: encouraging each to work and to support the others, so that resources reach everyone. A good society, like a good well, depends on maintenance and mutual aid.

lines.text: The well is muddy; no one drinks from it. At the old well, not even the animals come.
lines.meaning: Something good has been neglected until it has turned to mud. That may be your own skills, your health or a relationship you have let silt up. People stop coming to what no longer refreshes them. Do not blame them. If you feel ignored, ask whether you have let yourself go stale. Clean out the sediment and the water can run clear again.

lines.text: At the well hole, shooting at minnows. The jug is broken and leaks.
lines.meaning: The water is good but you are using it for small things, shooting at tiny fish instead of drawing water for people. Your talents are real but you are wasting them on trivial ends, or the means to share them are cracked. No one above draws on you, so you drift downward. Repair your vessel and turn your gifts toward something that truly matters.

lines.text: The well has been cleaned, but no one drinks from it. This grieves my heart, for the water could be drawn. If the king were clear-sighted, all would share the blessing.
lines.meaning: You are capable and ready, and your work is sound, but it goes unused and unrecognized. The frustration is real, and others who see it grieve on your behalf. The line places the fault with those who fail to notice, not with you. Keep the water clean. When someone with discernment comes along, your worth will benefit many people.

lines.text: The well is being lined with stone. No mistake.
lines.meaning: For now, the well is out of use while its walls are repaired. You cannot give much to others at the moment because you are working on yourself: learning, healing, putting your life in order. That is no fault. It is necessary maintenance. Without a firm lining, the well would collapse and the water would turn muddy. Do this work thoroughly; the time to serve will come.

lines.text: The well is clear: a cold spring, and people drink.
lines.meaning: This is the well at its best, the ruler of the hexagram. The water is pure and fresh, and it nourishes everyone who comes. You have something of real value to offer: knowledge, care, leadership. It is available and being used. Keep the source clean and the access open. A clear well needs to be drawn from; goodness is meant to be put to use.

lines.text: Water is drawn up from the well; do not cover it. Be trustworthy: supreme good fortune.
lines.meaning: The well has done its work and the water comes up for all. The instruction is not to close it off. Do not restrict what you have to those you favor or hoard it for yourself. Keep your source open to everyone who needs it, and be dependable. The more freely you give, the more the well fills. This is the highest good fortune.

life.work: Go deep enough to reach real substance, look after your tools and skills, and make your work available to those who need it.
life.love: Tend the shared source of the relationship: keep it clean, keep it open, and draw from it honestly.
life.inner: Return regularly to the deep, unchanging sources of wisdom, and clear out whatever silts them up.

question: Is your rope long enough to reach the water, or are you stopping just short of the source?

name: Revolution
essence: Something old has to be shed and replaced, the way an animal molts its coat. Change of this size succeeds only when its time has truly come and people can see why it is needed.

judgment.text: Revolution. Only when its day has come will people believe in it. Then there is great success, and it pays to stay steady and correct. Regret disappears.
judgment.meaning: The character for this hexagram first meant an animal’s hide, the pelt that is shed and grows back new each season. Revolution here is not chaos but a necessary molt: a form that no longer fits is replaced by one that does. The warning is about timing. If you push a sweeping change before others feel the need for it, it will be resisted and distrusted. Wait for its day, when the old way has plainly run out, and the change will carry people with it. Then it brings great success. Keep your motives clean and your methods fair, because a revolution judged by its results needs to be right as well as bold. Done this way, the regrets that usually follow upheaval fall away.

image.text: Fire inside the lake: the picture of Revolution. The wise person works out the calendar and makes the seasons clear.
image.meaning: Fire below and water above fight each other: the water may put out the fire, or the fire may boil the water dry. One must give way, and that struggle is the engine of change. The wise person responds not by stirring conflict but by reading the cycles, like an astronomer setting the calendar so people know when to plant and when to harvest. Understand the larger rhythm of change, and you will know when a turn is due.

lines.text: Bound tight in the hide of a yellow cow.
lines.meaning: At the very start, you are not in a position to change anything yet. Yellow is the color of the centre and of moderation, and the cow is docile: you are held, firmly, in patience. Do not act on your restlessness. Stay within your role, gather your understanding, and let the conditions ripen. Moving now would only expose a plan nobody is ready for.

lines.text: When the day has come, make the change. Going ahead brings good fortune. No mistake.
lines.meaning: This line sits in the centre of the fire trigram and is answered by the strong ruler in line 5. The preparation is done and the moment has arrived. Hesitating now would be the error. Make the change you have been readying, clearly and in good faith. You have support from above and the situation needs you to move. Good fortune, and no one can fault you.

lines.text: Charging ahead brings misfortune. Holding on stubbornly is also dangerous. When the talk of change has gone round three times, you can commit, and people will trust you.
lines.meaning: You are strong and restless at the top of the lower trigram, tempted either to force the change or to dig in against it. Both go badly. Instead, test the idea. Talk it through, listen, and let the case for change come round three times, until it has been examined from every side. Once it has held up and people have been heard, commit. That kind of change earns lasting trust.

lines.text: Regret disappears. With sincere trust, changing the mandate brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: The fourth line crosses from the lower to the upper trigram: the point where change actually takes hold. Here the old order can be replaced, the mandate itself rewritten, and it goes well because people already trust you. Your regrets fade because your aims are sound. Make sure the new arrangement truly serves the people it affects, not only your own vision, and the change will stand.

lines.text: The great person changes like a tiger. Even before consulting the oracle, they have the people’s trust.
lines.meaning: A tiger’s new coat comes in bold, clear stripes that anyone can see. This is the ruler’s line, strong and central. When change comes from someone of real character, its shape is obvious and its reasons speak for themselves. You do not need to argue or seek signs; people already believe in you. Lead the change openly, with confidence and clarity.

lines.text: The noble one changes like a leopard. Small-minded people change only their faces. Pushing further brings misfortune. Settling down and holding steady brings good fortune.
lines.meaning: The great turn is over. Those of good character now refine themselves, their patterns finer like a leopard’s spots. Others adjust only on the surface, going along outwardly. Accept that. Trying to force a deeper conversion on everyone would undo what was won. The work now is consolidation: let the new order settle, keep it steady, and stop pressing for more change.

life.work: A major restructuring, a pivot or a break with the old way is warranted, but only once the need is evident to others; prepare the case, then act decisively.
life.love: A relationship may need a real change in its terms, not just a patch; talk it through until you both see why, then change together.
life.inner: Let go of an old identity that no longer fits you, the way an animal sheds a coat, without forcing yourself before you are ready.

question: What in your life has outgrown its form, and has its day for change really come?

name: The Cauldron
essence: The sacred bronze cauldron cooks food for the community and offerings for the ancestors. It stands for what nourishes people at a deeper level, and for setting yourself rightly in your place so that higher purpose can work through you.

judgment.text: The Cauldron. Supreme good fortune and success.
judgment.meaning: The ding was the great ritual vessel of ancient China: three legs, two ears, a lid, often cast in bronze. In it, raw food became a meal and a sacrifice to heaven and to the ancestors; a dynasty’s cauldrons were symbols of its legitimacy. The hexagram even looks like one, with a broken bottom line for the legs, solid lines for the belly, a broken fifth line for the ears and a solid top line for the carrying bar. Where Revolution clears away the old, the Cauldron builds the new order: a culture, a team, a practice that feeds people. The omen is simply excellent. Your task is to be a sound vessel: well made, well placed, carrying something worth offering.

image.text: Fire burning over wood: the picture of the Cauldron. The wise person sets their position right and so makes their calling firm.
image.meaning: Wood feeds the flame and the flame cooks what is in the vessel; each part has its place and the whole transforms.
